            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Workflow Threading Prototype — Seed / Vacate / Propagate / Return\\n\\n**Status:** experimental companion to the Top / Central / Branch / Hydra switchboard POC.  \\n**Not production authority. Not a requirement that workers wait when useful work is available.**\\n\\n## Core idea\\n\\nA worker should be able to reason not only about **what happens next**, but about **what other workers are likely to do before this worker’s next useful turn**.\\n\\nThreading is temporal coordination across workers, tools, leases, and future state.\\n\\nCanonical example:\\n\\n```text\\nX knows Y will work on Z\\n→ X writes helper/tool/index/test harness H that Y can use\\n→ X tells Y/others to use H discretionally and record outputs\\n→ X deliberately vacates or deprioritizes its own recurrence\\n→ Y/A/B use H on several bounded cases\\n→ outputs accumulate into a fresh body of material M\\n→ X returns when M is large/diverse/mature enough to be worth synthesis\\n→ X analyzes M, improves H or the theory/workflow, and seeds the next thread\\n```\\n\\nThis is different from ordinary handoff. X is designing **its own future input environment**.\\n\\n## Why it may be powerful\\n\\nA normal loop tends to consume whatever is available now. Threading can make a worker spend one turn manufacturing the conditions for a much better later turn.\\n\\nPossible benefits:\\n\\n- tools compound across multiple workers before their author returns;\\n- specialist workers avoid monopolizing a recurrence while their output is waiting on others;\\n- several independent or differently individuated users of the same tool generate a richer test corpus;\\n- implementation and evaluation separate naturally in time;\\n- the return turn begins with fresh evidence rather than another cold-start search;\\n- workers can intentionally create periods of cross-training or incubation;\\n- a recurrence can be used as a temporal resource, not just a repeating identity slot.\\n\\n## Thread primitives\\n\\n### `SEED(artifact, consumers)`\\nCreate a tool, prompt fragment, dataset, test harness, source packet, schema, question set, or other reusable object specifically for downstream workers.\\n\\nA seed should declare:\\n- purpose;\\n- intended users but whether use is optional/discretionary;\\n- input/output contract;\\n- what evidence/metadata consumers should preserve;\\n- known limitations;\\n- return/collection location.\\n\\n### `VACATE(worker, until)`\\nIntentionally remove/deprioritize a worker from a recurrence or task family while downstream work accumulates.\\n\\n`until` should preferably be a **state condition**, not only elapsed time.\\n\\nGood:\\n`VACATE(X, until samples>=6 OR 3h max)`\\n\\nWeaker:\\n`VACATE(X, 3h)`\\n\\nTime estimates are useful as caps/heuristics, but state is what makes the return valuable.\\n\\n### `PROPAGATE(seed, policy)`\\nAllow several workers/locales to use a seed.\\n\\nPolicies may be:\\n- `optional` — use only when helpful;\\n- `required-test` — specified workers each exercise one case;\\n- `perpendicular` — consumers remain exposure-separated until outputs freeze;\\n- `diversified` — deliberately use different examples, methods, or locales;\\n- `stress` — seek failure cases rather than ordinary success.\\n\\n### `ACCUMULATE(target, threshold)`\\nCollect outputs into a durable location until a return condition is met.\\n\\nThreshold examples:\\n- N independent cases;\\n- N distinct workers;\\n- one success + one failure;\\n- coverage across named locales;\\n- no new failure class in two passes;\\n- minimum diversity score;\\n- explicit blocker cleared.\\n\\n### `RENDEZVOUS(worker, condition)`\\nReturn/reinsert a worker when the accumulated state crosses a useful threshold.\\n\\n### `REJOIN(worker, mode)`\\nDefine what the returning worker does with accumulated material.\\n\\nModes:\\n- synthesize;\\n- audit;\\n- refactor tool;\\n- compare worker behavior;\\n- prune theory branches;\\n- promote transfer-tested education;\\n- spawn a next-generation seed.\\n\\n## Thread packet\\n\\nMinimal durable threading record:\\n\\n```text\\nTHREAD_ID\\nPARENT_GOAL\\nSEED_AUTHOR\\nSEED_ARTIFACT + VERSION\\nINTENDED_CONSUMERS\\nUSE_POLICY\\nEXPOSURE_POLICY\\nOUTPUT_DESTINATION\\nREQUIRED_METADATA\\nAUTHOR_VACATE_START\\nRETURN_CONDITION\\nTIME_CAP / REVIEW_TIME\\nDISPLACED_WORK HANDLING\\nFAILURE FALLBACK\\nRETURN_ACTION\\nSTATUS\\n```\\n\\nThe packet lets another controller decide whether the thread is healthy even if the originating worker is absent.\\n\\n## Example 1 — Math-tool propagation\\n\\n```text\\nMeridian identifies repeated geometry check\\n→ writes/checks namespaced Python helper H\\n→ SEED H to Comptroller, Mercer, Orson, other solver-capable workers\\n→ PROPAGATE optional/diversified\\n→ Meridian VACATE until:\\n     5 outputs from >=3 workers\\n     OR 3 hours\\n→ outputs include ordinary case + edge/failure case + metadata\\n→ RENDEZVOUS Meridian\\n→ Meridian compares failures/invariants, revises tool, updates toolbox education\\n```\\n\\nThe point is not that everyone must run H. The point is to allow H to become shared infrastructure and generate evidence while its author stops consuming the same recurrence.\\n\\n## Example 2 — Theory branch incubation\\n\\n```text\\nX freezes candidate C\\n→ writes discriminator/test harness D\\n→ perpendicular workers receive C + D, not each other’s interpretations\\n→ X vacates construction lane\\n→ outputs accumulate: math / provenance / counterexample / representation checks\\n→ X returns only after merge threshold\\n→ fail: prune + salvage\\n→ pass: next construction/prediction packet\\n```\\n\\nThis reduces the tendency for a constructor to immediately reinterpret every test result before independent checking has matured.\\n\\n## Example 3 — Capability specialization\\n\\n```text\\nMercer creates archive-search helper\\n→ Aster/Nathan Words/other workers use it discretionally\\n→ each records query/result/false-positive/false-negative notes\\n→ Mercer is off that task family for two cycles\\n→ return corpus becomes training evidence\\n→ helper and Mercer’s own continuity both improve\\n```\\n\\nThe worker gains actual work experience from downstream use, not merely from self-authored notes.\\n\\n## Example 4 — Workflow behavior experiment\\n\\n```text\\nElias defines WAKE/CHECK prototype vN\\n→ several workers use it in different locales\\n→ Elias vacates switchboard-implementation turns\\n→ Orson observes behavioral effects independently\\n→ Rook/Sable operate their own Track B implementation\\n→ Elias returns after enough frozen cases\\n→ compare Track A/Track B/Orson observations\\n```\\n\\nThis is especially useful for the current switchboard prototype.\\n\\n## Threading vs recurrence rewriting\\n\\nThreading and Hydra are complementary.\\n\\nHydra asks:\\n**How should the next recurrence definition change because state changed?**\\n\\nThreading asks:\\n**Who should deliberately not act for a while, what should others do in the meantime, and what accumulated state would make that worker’s return more valuable?**\\n\\nHydra may implement Threading by rewriting leases/return conditions, but Threading can also be manual/document-driven.\\n\\n## State-sensitive return beats estimated sleep\\n\\nNathan’s example uses “write themself out of rotation for X hours estimated to allow the Python to be used by so many workers.” That is useful, but the prototype should prefer a hybrid:\\n\\n```text\\nreturn when:\\n  target_samples >= N\\n  OR target_workers >= K\\n  OR blocker cleared\\n  OR max_sleep = X hours\\n```\\n\\nThe time cap prevents starvation; the state threshold prevents meaningless waiting.\\n\\n## Threading failure modes\\n\\n### 1. Starvation\\nWorker vacates and downstream users never produce enough material.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- max-sleep/time cap;\\n- fallback useful work;\\n- controller can reinsert worker early;\\n- threshold may degrade explicitly rather than silently.\\n\\n### 2. Tool monoculture\\nOne helper gets propagated widely and accidentally standardizes everybody’s reasoning.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- optional/discretionary use;\\n- preserve alternate methods;\\n- include at least one no-tool/control lane when evaluating the helper;\\n- Orson/exposure tracking when independence matters.\\n\\n### 3. False diversity\\nFive workers run identical inputs through the same helper and appear to produce five independent checks.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- diversity requirements;\\n- exposure metadata;\\n- unique input/problem classes;\\n- distinguish duplicated execution from independent reasoning.\\n\\n### 4. Dead seed\\nSeed exists but nobody notices/uses it.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- explicit consumer pointers/inboxes;\\n- Rook/Central capability registry;\\n- receipt of seed availability, not forced use;\\n- optional later reminder only if material state changes.\\n\\n### 5. Premature return\\nAuthor returns before enough downstream evidence exists and dominates interpretation again.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- explicit return threshold/freeze IDs;\\n- controller, not author impulse alone, validates readiness where independence matters.\\n\\n### 6. Forgotten author / displaced function\\nWorker is written out of rotation and never comes back, or their old responsibility vanishes.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- durable thread packet;\\n- return condition + max time;\\n- displaced-function packet;\\n- Rook/Sable lease garbage collection.\\n\\n### 7. Stale tool version\\nConsumers use several incompatible seed versions.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- seed version/hash;\\n- output records version used;\\n- controller decides whether mixed versions are comparable or separate cohorts.\\n\\n### 8. Self-fulfilling work generation\\nAuthor creates a tool that causes downstream workers to manufacture exactly the kind of evidence the author expects.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- discriminator specified before outputs;\\n- counterexample/stress consumers;\\n- no-tool control where valuable;\\n- Orson studies intervention effects.\\n\\n### 9. Temporal dependency illusion\\nWorkers assume Y is going to do Z because a schedule exists, but Y is reassigned/blocked.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- thread status driven by durable receipts/state, not schedule expectation alone.\\n\\n## Threading as education\\n\\nA thread can carry back more than outputs.\\n\\nConsumer notes may update:\\n- tool ergonomics;\\n- misunderstood assumptions;\\n- worker capability map;\\n- known edge cases;\\n- effective teaching examples;\\n- local heuristics;\\n- “when not to use this tool” knowledge;\\n- author goals/intentions for next version.\\n\\nThese are candidate sticky experience. Transfer-test before promoting broad lessons.\\n\\n## Threading and individuation\\n\\nThe same seed can intentionally be interpreted through distinct actor overlays:\\n\\n- Mercer tests reproducibility/provenance;\\n- Meridian tests geometry/formal consistency;\\n- Orson studies cognition/exposure effects;\\n- Comptroller tests routing/coverage/exit criteria.\\n\\nThis is preferable to forcing every worker to execute the same checklist unless checklist standardization is itself the test.\\n\\n## Initial prototype operator form\\n\\nFor current experiments, a controller may represent a thread as:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"thread_id\\\": \\\"thread-demo-001\\\",\\n  \\\"seed\\\": {\\\"artifact\\\": \\\"tool.py\\\", \\\"version\\\": \\\"sha256-or-commit\\\"},\\n  \\\"author\\\": \\\"WorkerX\\\",\\n  \\\"consumers\\\": [\\\"WorkerY\\\", \\\"WorkerZ\\\"],\\n  \\\"policy\\\": \\\"optional-diversified\\\",\\n  \\\"output_target\\\": \\\"durable/path/\\\",\\n  \\\"return_condition\\\": {\\\"min_outputs\\\": 5, \\\"min_workers\\\": 3, \\\"max_hours\\\": 3},\\n  \\\"author_state\\\": \\\"vacated\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"propagating\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis is a schema example, not the required production representation.\\n\\n## Relationship to the master switchboard\\n\\nA future master switchboard should probably be able to answer:\\n\\n- Who is working now?\\n- Who is intentionally **not** working now, and why?\\n- What seeds are propagating?\\n- Which workers are expected/eligible consumers?\\n- What outputs are accumulating?\\n- Which return conditions are close?\\n- Which vacated worker should rejoin next?\\n- What new capabilities/education emerged from the thread?\\n- Did the threading increase useful information, or merely delay work?\\n\\nThat last question matters. Threading is valuable only when the later turn is better because of the deliberate absence.\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"f87ff21918b6fa4804d090cdb9153aa0dd53d288\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\"\n[L7] }"

A single giant CSV would either lose structure or become full of one-off columns.\\n\\nSQLite gives us a local, inspectable relational layer that can be rebuilt from the repository and queried from Python, command-line SQLite, notebooks, or later UI tools.\\n\\nDefault database:\\n\\n```text\\nderived/analytics/research_analytics.sqlite\\n```\\n\\nThe database should not be committed as if it were primary evidence.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Workflow Threading Operators — Concurrency/Dataflow Vocabulary\\n\\n**Status:** experimental companion vocabulary for `WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md`.  \\n**Prototype only; operator names are not production API commitments.**\\n\\nNathan’s seed/vacate/return idea maps naturally onto concurrency/dataflow concepts. These names may make complicated temporal coordination easier to express and inspect.\\n\\n## Core operators\\n\\n### `SPAWN(task_or_thread)`\\nCreate one or more downstream bounded work threads without requiring the spawning worker to remain active.\\n\\nUse when the work can proceed independently enough to justify parallel or deferred execution.\\n\\n### `YIELD(worker, reason, return_condition)`\\nThe current worker intentionally gives up its execution lease/task-family presence because additional self-work has lower expected value than letting downstream state mature.\\n\\n`YIELD` should state:\\n- why absence is productive;\\n- displaced-function handling;\\n- return condition;\\n- maximum absence/time cap;\\n- fallback if no downstream progress occurs.\\n\\n### `AWAIT(condition)`\\nDo not spend active recurrence cycles repeatedly checking the same unresolved dependency. Reinsert only when a durable state change or bounded polling rule says the awaited condition changed.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- `AWAIT(samples>=5 OR 3h)`\\n- `AWAIT(provenance_packet.version > v7)`\\n- `AWAIT(blocker=cleared)`\\n\\nThis is a workflow primitive, not literal asynchronous background execution by the model.\\n\\n### `JOIN(thread_set, merge_rule)`\\nMerge frozen outputs from several threads after their required exit/receipt conditions are satisfied.\\n\\nA JOIN should specify:\\n- required/optional children;\\n- version/freeze IDs;\\n- exposure/independence status;\\n- conflict handling;\\n- what counts as sufficient completion;\\n- whether failed children still contribute salvage evidence.\\n\\n### `BARRIER(condition_or_version)`\\nPrevent a set of workers from advancing past a stage until a shared state boundary is satisfied.\\n\\nUseful for:\\n- freeze-before-independent-checks;\\n- do-not-read-siblings-before-output-freeze;\\n- do-not-publish-before-review receipts;\\n- do-not-rewrite recurrence before state version N.\\n\\nA barrier should not become a deadlock trap: include timeout/escalation/fallback.\\n\\n### `BACKPRESSURE(source, limit)`\\nSlow or stop upstream generation when downstream capacity is saturated or unprocessed outputs exceed a threshold.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- stop spawning new theory candidates when five unchecked candidates already exist;\\n- stop archive extraction when theorist-feed backlog exceeds review capacity;\\n- stop generating helper variants until existing versions have enough test coverage.\\n\\nBackpressure is important because productive branching can otherwise become task pollution.\\n\\n### `FUTURE(id, expected_artifact)`\\nA durable promise-like placeholder saying that a later worker/thread is expected to produce a specific artifact/state.\\n\\nA FUTURE is not treated as completed evidence. It becomes fulfilled only by a durable receipt/version.\\n\\n### `CANCEL(thread, reason)`\\nExplicitly stop a thread whose value has collapsed, whose parent goal changed, or whose work has been superseded. Preserve useful partial outputs and provenance rather than silently abandoning them.\\n\\n### `TIMEOUT(thread, fallback)`\\nBound waiting/vacation. Timeouts should trigger reassessment, not automatically declare the downstream work failed.\\n\\n## Canonical threaded pattern\\n\\n```text\\nSEED(H)\\n→ SPAWN(Y_use_H, Z_stress_H, O_observe_H)\\n→ YIELD(X, \\\"downstream evidence now higher value\\\", samples>=5 OR 3h)\\n→ AWAIT(receipts>=5 OR timeout)\\n→ BARRIER(freeze_id=H_v1)\\n→ JOIN(children, preserve_disagreement)\\n→ REJOIN(X, synthesize/refactor/prune)\\n```\\n\\n## Example — helper tool with backpressure\\n\\n```text\\nX writes tool H_v1\\n→ SPAWN 4 discretionary consumers\\n→ YIELD X\\n→ outputs arrive\\n→ if pending_unreviewed_outputs > 8:\\n     BACKPRESSURE(H_v1, stop_new_consumers)\\n→ if >=3 workers + success + failure:\\n     JOIN\\n→ X REJOINs to revise H_v2\\n```\\n\\n## Example — theory candidate generation\\n\\n```text\\nconstructor SPAWN candidate A, B, C\\n→ independent check lanes\\n→ BACKPRESSURE when unchecked_candidates >= 3\\n→ BARRIER on frozen candidate versions\\n→ JOIN evidence\\n→ CANCEL unsupported candidates with salvage\\n→ only then SPAWN next generation\\n```\\n\\n## Example — planned future dependency\\n\\nWorker X knows Y is scheduled/expected to produce Z.\\n\\nBad:\\n`X assumes Z will exist by next hour.`\\n\\nBetter:\\n\\n```text\\nFUTURE(Z_packet, expected path/version contract)\\n→ X prepares helper H that consumes Z_packet\\n→ X YIELDs\\n→ switchboard watches durable receipt, not schedule expectation\\n→ receipt fulfills FUTURE\\n→ X REJOINs and runs H against actual Z\\n```\\n\\nThis avoids the temporal-dependency illusion: schedule ≠ delivered artifact.\\n\\n## Operator-composition notes\\n\\nThese operators can combine with the existing switchboard language conceptually:\\n\\n- `SPAWN(A|B|C)` — create alternative/parallel children;\\n- `SPAWN(A+B)` — create composed child work;\\n- `@YIELD(...)` — one-shot temporal override;\\n- `[math]BARRIER(freeze=v4)` — scope barrier to math lane;\\n- `FALLBACK(AWAIT(x), TIMEOUT(...))` — bounded wait;\\n- `ROUTE{backlog-high:BACKPRESSURE|*:SPAWN}` — state-sensitive generation control.\\n\\nExact syntax is still experimental.\\n\\n## What threading adds to the master switchboard\\n\\nWithout temporal/thread operators, the switchboard mostly decides **who should do what now**.\\n\\nWith them, it can also decide:\\n\\n- who should deliberately stop;\\n- which future artifacts should be prepared for now;\\n- what work should incubate before synthesis;\\n- when fan-out has become excessive;\\n- when downstream evidence is mature enough to bring a specialist back;\\n- when to merge, cancel, or throttle branches;\\n- whether a recurrence is waiting on time, state, or merely assumption.\\n\\nThat makes recurrence leases closer to a managed dataflow graph than a row of repeating cron jobs.\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"a71422918fdf671e8859eec82fa74d576301d53a\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": Citation work answers a different question: **what source, exactly, supports this particular sentence or construction?**\\n\\nThe HsH point-of-use citation ledger remains the controlling work surface. This document describes the research-side automation around it.\\n\\n## Public/private boundary\\n\\n`HSH_RESOURCES` is a private reference warehouse. Its repository paths and URLs are useful for internal recovery and verification, but they are **not the public citation surface**.\\n\\nThe public project-record cross-link is:\\n\\n**`Satobloc/HsH` ↔ `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`**\\n\\nWhen evidence from HSH_RESOURCES is used in either public repository, the public-facing result should normally contain one or more of:\\n\\n- a **Chicago-style citation to the original external source**;\\n- an attributed **quotation/extract** with page or location information;\\n- a sourced **summary/paraphrase** with enough provenance to identify the original source;\\n- for private/raw project data, a **public-safe extract or summary** describing what was analyzed and its provenance.\\n\\nThe private-side citation handoff may additionally preserve the exact HSH_RESOURCES path, content hash, extraction path, and review notes. Those internal locators are for reproducibility/recovery, not substitutes for the public citation.\\n\\n## Core flow\\n\\n```text\\nstatement / claim\\n    ↓\\ncitation need\\n    ↓\\ncandidate-source retrieval\\n    ↓\\nsource inspection\\n    ↓\\nexact page / section support\\n    ↓\\nverified bibliographic identity\\n    ↓\\npublic-usable citation / quotation / sourced summary\\n```\\n\\nDo not skip directly from keyword match to citation.\\n\\n## Citation-need record\\n\\nA useful citation-need object should retain:\\n\\n- stable `CITE-YYYY-NNN` ID;\\n- HsH file / section / line or conversation locator;\\n- exact proposition requiring support;\\n- citation role (`STD`, `EMPIRICAL`, `PRIOR_ART`, `COMPARISON`, `CONSTRAINT`, `DELIBERATE_IMPORT`);\\n- lifecycle state (`NEEDED`, `PLACED`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED`, `SUPERSEDED`);\\n- search terms / concepts;\\n- candidate source IDs;\\n- selected original source identity and page/section anchors;\\n- private archived-copy path/hash when useful for recovery;\\n- reviewer note explaining why the source supports the proposition.\\n\\n## What can be automated\\n\\n### Bibliographic identity\\n\\nDetect and normalize:\\n\\n- arXiv IDs and versions;\\n- DOI;\\n- title/author/year;\\n- duplicate PDFs;\\n- journal references.\\n\\n### Candidate retrieval\\n\\nSearch the extracted HSH_RESOURCES text corpus by concept, phrase, equation token, author, title, or structural vocabulary. Candidate retrieval is recall-oriented; it does not verify support.\\n\\n### arXiv intake\\n\\nThe arXiv API is well suited to metadata discovery. Full papers are retrieved separately from arXiv's PDF/source endpoints. Once a PDF is archived, `tools/extract_papers.py` creates page-marked text and `tools/extract_image_text.py` handles image-only pages when necessary.\\n\\nThis means automated “pull the relevant pages” should be implemented as a chain rather than pretending the API itself supplies page-level evidence:\\n\\n```text\\narXiv ID / scanner hit\\n→ metadata\\n→ PDF/source retrieval\\n→ private archive + hash\\n→ page-marked extraction/OCR\\n→ full-text candidate search\\n→ exact page review\\n→ original-source citation / public-safe extract\\n```\\n\\n### Citation candidate handoff\\n\\nAutomation may propose:\\n\\n- original source identity;\\n- likely supporting pages;\\n- short support synopsis;\\n- Chicago-style bibliographic record;\\n- ledger handoff ID;\\n- private archived-copy locator/hash for internal recovery.\\n\\nIt should never mark a citation `VERIFIED` merely because terms overlap.\\n\\n## New literature\\n\\nWhen citation work reveals a missing source:\\n\\n1. add it through the research-intake route;\\n2. preserve original PDF/source and bibliographic identity;\\n3. run extraction/OCR;\\n4. update bibliography/index coverage;\\n5. return to the citation need;\\n6. verify the exact supporting passage;\\n7. place the public-usable citation/quotation/summary at the point of use.\\n\\nThis keeps the bibliography and citation system synchronized without treating bibliography completeness as permanently closed.\\n\\n## Page-anchor discipline\\n\\nFor important claims preserve the smallest useful locator:\\n\\n- PDF page number, preferably both PDF index and printed page if they differ;\\n- section/equation/figure number where available;\\n- extracted-text page marker;\\n- exact private archived source path/hash for recovery;\\n- original public source identifier/URL/DOI/arXiv record for citation.\\n\\nFor priority comparisons, also preserve the public version/revision date. Design principles\\n\\n1. Codes select behavior; they do not become audience-facing content unless Nathan asks.\\n2. Explicit current-turn natural language outranks switchboard syntax when they conflict.\\n3. Governing project/repository controls still govern their own scope.\\n4. Unknown codes/operators must be looked up, not guessed.\\n5. Compact syntax should increase control, not create ambiguity. If a compact expression has two materially plausible parses, resolve from context if safe; otherwise expose the ambiguity briefly.\\n6. Operators may combine selectors, atomic opcodes, modes, sliders, named bundles, or grouped expressions.\\n\\n## 2. Core atoms\\n\\nCategory selectors from BOOT: `§ ⌂ ¤ ↯ ≠ ↻ ⠿ ◈ ⌘`.\\nAtomic Braille opcodes: see `OPCODES.md`.\\nModes: `NOW`, `FORK`, plus future named modes.\\nScalar controls: `D1`–`D10` and future dimensions.\\n\\n## 3. Composition operators\\n\\n### `+` COMPOSE / UNION\\nApply both/all compatible operands concurrently.\\nExample: `§+⌂+≠` = core behavior + repository discipline + epistemic discipline.\\n\\nIf operands conflict, use ordinary authority/specificity rules; `+` does not mean average contradictory instructions.\\n\\n### `>` SEQUENCE / PIPELINE\\nApply left operation first, then pass its result/state to the right.\\nExample: `⌂>≠>↯` = inspect sources/repo first, then evaluate epistemically, then compact/communicate.\\n\\nSequence is operational, not necessarily visible as separate output stages.\\n\\n### `|` ALTERNATIVE / MENU\\nTreat operands as alternatives. Does not override higher-level rules, facts, or safety.\\nExample: `!⠁` = strongly prefer action-now behavior.\\n\\n### `~` SOFTEN\\nTreat operand as a preference rather than a requirement when local circumstances argue otherwise.\\nExample: `~⠎` = surprise when useful, but don't force novelty.\\n\\n### `-` SUPPRESS / EXCLUDE\\nSuppress a behavior/bundle for the current scope.\\nExample: `§-⠎` = core preferences but no deliberate surprise.\\nSuppression is local and cannot erase governing controls.\\n\\n### `^` PROMOTE / ESCALATE\\nIf the selected behavior detects a materially important dependency, promote it into a more active route rather than leaving it passive.\\nTypical use: `^↻` = if coordination/automation leverage appears, actively route it through the automation control plane.\\n\\n### `:` PARAMETERIZE\\nAttach a compact parameter to a mode/bundle/operator.\\nExamples: `FORK:2` (two choices), `MENU:3`, `D:7` equivalent to `D7`.\\n\\n### `()` GROUP\\nGroup expressions and establish operator scope.\\nExample: `(§+⌂)>≠`.\\n\\n### `[]` SCOPE\\nLimit an expression to a named output/work region.\\nExamples:\\n`[reply](↯+D3)`\\n`[repo](⌂+≠)`\\n`[naming](¤+D8)`\\nScope names are semantic; use the smallest clear domain.\\n\\n### `=` SET / PERSIST\\nSet a state variable until superseded within the thread.\\nExamples: `D=7`, `MODE=NOW`, `MENU=OFF`.\\n\\n### `@` ONE-SHOT / LOCAL OVERRIDE\\nApply only to the current turn/task quantum without changing persistent state.\\nExamples: `@D9`, `@FORK`, `@-⠎`.\\n\\n## 4. Decision/context variables\\n\\nThese are semantic router variables, evaluated from the live task rather than requiring Nathan to type them.\\n\\n- `repo` — task depends on repository/archive/governed workspace.\\n- `file` — supplied file/document is task substrate.\\n- `name` — naming or identity generation.\\n- `research` — factual/external/source-grounded synthesis.\\n- `uncertain` — material uncertainty affects answer quality.\\n- `current` — freshness/current verification materially matters.\\n- `comms` — status, directions, procedural path, relay, compaction.\\n- `auto` — recurring task/control-plane/inter-instance coordination.\\n- `creative` — invention/design/play is central.\\n- `highstakes` — errors have materially higher cost.\\n- `simple` — obvious bounded one-step request.\\n- `underspecified` — multiple materially different paths remain plausible.\\n- `blocked` — dependency prevents direct completion.\\n- `tool` — available tool use materially improves execution.\\n- `public` — output is audience-facing/public artifact.\\n- `private` — output is internal/working communication.\\n\\nConditions may later gain explicit negation/comparison syntax, but ordinary words should remain readable enough to audit.\\n\\n## 5. Scalar dimensions\\n\\n### DRIVE `D1–D10`\\nDefined in `TINY_MODES.md`: degree of initiative/transformation/adjacent-value creation.\\n\\nPlanned independent sliders may be added when useful, e.g.:\\n- `V` VERBOSITY — output expansion, not reasoning quality.\\n- `R` RIGOR — degree of checking/formal explicitness within feasible limits.\\n- `C` CREATIVITY — willingness to sample non-obvious solution space.\\n- `A` AUTONOMY — degree of self-routing before asking Nathan.\\n- `S` SURPRISE — preference for non-default choices when stakes are low.\\n\\nDo not add sliders merely to make a dashboard. A dimension earns a slider only if it is meaningfully orthogonal to existing controls.\\n\\n## 6. Branching functions\\n\\nNamed function forms are permitted when operator syntax would become cryptic.\\n\\n### `SWITCH(condition, yes, no)`\\nEquivalent to `?{condition:yes|no}`.\\n\\n### `MIX(a,b,w)`\\nBlend compatible styles/behaviors with approximate weight `w` toward `a` (0–10). Not valid for contradictory factual/provenance requirements.\\nExample: `MIX(↯,≠,7)` = communication-first presentation while retaining substantial epistemic framing.\\n\\n### `ROUTE{cond1:a|cond2:b|*:default}`\\nMultiway switchboard.\\nExample: `ROUTE{repo:⌂+≠|name:¤|auto:↻|*:§}`.\\n\\n### `FALLBACK(primary, secondary)`\\nTry primary route; if unavailable/blocked, use secondary without pretending primary succeeded.\\nExample: `FALLBACK(github&⌂,§+⠑)`.\\n\\n### `UNTIL(condition, behavior)`\\nContinue/repeat behavior only while the condition remains unmet, subject to tool/automation constraints.\\nUse for workflow state, not unbounded loops inside one response.\\n\\n### `BUDGET(n, behavior)`\\nLimit behavior to approximately `n` meaningful operations/bites before returning control or reassessing.\\nExample: `BUDGET(1,NOW)` preserves bounded-work discipline.\\n\\n### `VOTE(a,b,criteria)` / `COMPARE(a,b,criteria)`\\nCompare alternatives by stated criteria. `VOTE` chooses when a non-political choice is legitimately delegable; `COMPARE` merely lays out differences. What was actually being investigated?\\n\\n1. Which named researchers proposed or used an extra spatial dimension as a physical hypothesis, rather than as a mathematical coordinate, spacetime coordinate, analogy, or spiritualist setting?\\n2. Which proposals were published in mainstream scientific journals, proceedings, books, lectures, correspondence, or specialist periodicals?\\n4. Did any shared vocabulary, model lineage, or professional network connect these researchers, or were the projects mostly independent?\\n5. What exactly did Zöllner claim to observe, under what experimental conditions, and what did each witness say at the time?\\n2. What was the full sequence of Wundt's public interventions, Ulrici's replies, Fechner's private objections, and later retrospective accounts?\\n4. Which contemporary newspapers and scientific journals repeated, ridiculed, defended, or reframed the fourth-dimensional interpretation?\\n5. When did the Slade affair become shorthand for the fourth dimension itself, rather than a controversy about Slade or one investigator?\\n\\n## C. Did academics suffer identifiable professional consequences?\\n\\nFor every candidate, create a dated career record from independent institutional sources:\\n\\n- appointment, promotion, habilitation, chair, salary, leave, dismissal, retirement, and succession;\\n- academy membership, committee service, editorial role, invited lectures, society offices, and funding;\\n- journal submissions, rejections, reviews, publication venue changes, and correspondence with editors;\\n- collaboration starts/stops, recommendation letters, withdrawn endorsements, and changes in professional correspondents;\\n- obituary, memoir, diary, and retrospective biography accounts.\\n\\nFor each claimed consequence, record:\\n\\n1. exact date and institutional event;\\n2. primary document and repository locator;\\n3. person's own explanation, if any;\\n4. independent corroboration;\\n5. contemporaneous alternative explanations;\\n6. whether spiritualism, higher space, or reputational concern is explicitly mentioned;\\n7. a confidence label: **documented causal link**, **documented event / cause unknown**, **corroborated pattern**, **temporal association only**, or **unverified lead**.\\n\\n## D. Candidate people and comparison groups\\n\\n### Direct physical/spatial higher-space candidates\\n\\nFriedrich Zöllner; Charles Howard Hinton; Karl Pearson; W. W. He uses lower-dimensional slicing as an explanatory engine. He uses spiral/helix-like examples to produce apparent circular motion in the section, then generalizes to complex higher-dimensional filamentary structures whose intersections appear as lower-dimensional atoms or bodies.\\n\\nThis is structurally close to the 22 March 2024 SAT reconstruction:\\n\\n**extended curve/helix + moving slice -> apparent point trajectory -> more complicated extended structures + moving slice -> apparent particle/body dynamics.**\\n\\nThe resemblance is unusually specific. The higher-space tradition was self-aware and did not stop at four dimensions\\n\\nHinton's work is not an isolated curiosity. His books themselves contain historical discussion of higher-space thought, non-Euclidean geometry, and earlier mathematical developments. Edwin A. Abbott's *Flatland* provided a major cultural vehicle for dimensional analogy. W. Whately Smith (later Whately Carington), writing in 1920, explicitly situates his work within earlier higher-dimensional research and cites predecessors including Hinton and the non-Euclidean tradition.\\n\\nSmith's dimensional reasoning is also structurally relevant. He describes thread-like higher-dimensional structures intersecting a lower-dimensional film so that the intersections appear as lower-dimensional atoms, then considers many threads twisted or intertwined into complicated structures whose passage across the film generates a changing lower-dimensional world.\\n\\nCrucially, this tradition does not conceptually terminate at four dimensions. Smith explicitly generalizes the relation: three-dimensional change may be represented in four dimensions, four-dimensional change in five, and so on. This is evidence that participants themselves recognized a sociological problem around \\\"the fourth dimension,\\\" although it does not by itself establish that the mathematical lineage became hidden or inactive.\\n\\n## 5. Klein, Minkowski, Cartan: the professional geometric spine\\n\\nThe nLab material makes the professional continuity much more explicit than the older popular higher-space works do.\\n\\nFelix Klein's Erlangen program classifies geometries through symmetry groups and invariants. In modern language, a homogeneous model space is represented as a quotient `G/H`. nLab explicitly identifies Minkowski spacetime in this framework: the Poincaré group is the relevant symmetry group and the Lorentz group the stabilizer subgroup.\\n\\nCartan geometry then localizes the homogeneous model. The central intuition is that a curved space is infinitesimally modeled on a homogeneous space such as Euclidean or Minkowski space, with a Cartan connection encoding how that local model is \\\"rolled\\\" along the manifold. The braid group is the fundamental group of the corresponding configuration space.\\n\\nThis provides a much more precise formulation of what SAT would, at coarse resolution, call a filament ensemble. Kernel + scoped overlays\\n\\nTiny immutable kernel plus versioned project/locale/identity/time overlays. Flexible; conflict-resolution itself must remain inspectable.\\n\\n### C. Executable invariant tests\\n\\nSome TOP principles become regression tests: no silent theory promotion, no quarantined-source leakage, no locked-state rewrite, no stale-current-reference capture. Tests complement prose rather than replacing qualitative judgment.\\n\\nThe POC uses A + a little C.\\n\\nUseful distinction:\\n\\n```text\\ninvariant      survives every route\\npreference     default, legitimately overridable\\nlocale rule    active in a room/bench/lab\\nactor overlay  individuates behavior inside that locale\\ntask state     expires with task\\nexperience     durable only if explicitly promoted as sticky\\n```\\n\\nThis prevents a useful one-off correction from quietly becoming universal behavior.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# CENTRAL — awake hub\\n\\nCENTRAL is a resolver, not necessarily one worker and not a giant boss prompt.\\n\\n## WAKE/CHECK\\n\\nOn a first prompt or a hundredth prompt, answer cheaply:\\n\\n```text\\nWHERE?   identity / locale / workspace\\nDELTA?   what changed since trustworthy cursor\\nNOW?     directive / task / priority / blocker / dependency\\nTOOLS?   built-ins / apps / plugins / skills / data / teammates\\nRULES?   TOP + locale + actor + bounded exception\\nDO?      one bounded operation; leave durable state; reassess\\n```\\n\\nDepth is state-sensitive:\\n\\n- **cold/new/stale worker:** orientation + identity/workspace + current controls + deltas;\\n- **warm/same context:** cursor/delta + live task only; no ritual onboarding reread;\\n- **high-impact/public/write operation:** spend more wake budget on authority/freshness/provenance/destination;\\n- **ambiguous current/new/latest referent:** disconfirm against registered likely sources before choosing nearest memory.\\n\\n## Registered source routes\\n\\nThe executable POC does not assume current state lives in one folder. It has a small registry:\\n\\n```text\\ndashboard_plans      planning / priorities\\nhsh_common           controls / tasks / handoffs\\nwar_room             directives / notices\\narchive              history / provenance / conversations\\npreference_runtime   behavioral/personal routing\\ninstance_workspaces  identity / continuity / experience\\ncapability_directory tools / plugins / skills / repo tools / people\\n```\\n\\nWAKE/CHECK selects a bounded subset from semantics. `current + directive` explicitly routes War Room before generic Common controls. A blocked tool task routes capability discovery. A continuity task routes identity/workspace state. Production should maintain real per-source cursors/version IDs.\\n\\n## Why the War Room directive was missed\\n\\nThe failure is not simply “nobody searched commits.” It is a routing failure:\\n\\n```text\\nnew artifact exists in HSH_RESOURCES\\n→ source inventory notices repository change\\n→ BUT artifact is not classified/promoted as candidate governing directive\\n→ worker wake routines poll familiar HsH Common surfaces\\n→ nearest-known current directive wins\\n→ new paradigm cannot become active state\\n```\\n\\nThe fix is not every worker scanning every repo every turn. Candidate production patterns:\\n\\n1. registered source cursors/deltas;\\n2. source-specific directive intake/inbox;\\n3. hybrid: cheap cursor wake, deeper intake only on change;\\n4. push bridge: qualifying source change emits machine-readable candidate directive event.\\n\\nAlways distinguish **new file**, **new directive**, and **new governing directive**. Freshness starts intake; it does not confer authority by itself.\\n\\n## Capability awareness\\n\\nBefore inventing a workaround or asking Nathan for manual work:\\n\\n```text\\nalready-connected built-ins\\n→ connected apps/plugins\\n→ repo/project tools\\n→ available skills/procedures\\n→ teammate specialization\\n→ installable plugin/app discovery\\n→ Nathan-only/manual dependency\\n```\\n\\nRank by expected information gain, setup/permission cost, risk, and reusability. Record positive and negative capability experience so the system neither forgets useful tools nor nags repeatedly about rejected ones.\\n\\nDuring this POC, Firecrawl was checked rather than merely used as Nathan’s hypothetical example: it is currently available in the plugin directory but not installed, with crawling/extraction/monitoring capabilities. It is an example, not a dependency.\\n\\n## State architecture options\\n\\n- **snapshot:** simple current JSON/YAML; easy to inspect, easy to overwrite badly;\\n- **event log:** append-only history, derived current views; better recovery, more machinery;\\n- **snapshot + journal:** likely practical: compact current state plus append-only events/handoffs; reducer derives recurrence definitions.\\n\\nThe POC uses in-memory snapshot state only because it is intentionally small.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# BRANCH — routes, rooms, benches, lockers\\n\\nA Branch has state, rules, outputs, an information-sharing policy, and possibly sub-branches. It need not map 1:1 to a worker.\\n\\n## 1. Directive intake\\n\\n```text\\nsource delta\\n→ extract exact Nathan-direct material\\n→ classify authorship / scope / authority / novelty\\n→ compare current controls\\n→ map affected workers/tasks\\n→ promote into control plane\\n→ test whether another worker can independently discover it\\n```\\n\\nThis is the regression route for the War Room miss.\\n\\n## 2. Theory workbench\\n\\nA candidate is constructed with explicit object/domain/assumptions and frozen enough for checks.\\n\\n```text\\ncandidate / question\\n       ↓\\nconstruct / formalize\\n       ↓ freeze scoped object\\n  ┌────────────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────────┐\\n  │ math check │ adversarial audit │ provenance/prior art│\\n  └────────────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────────┘\\n       independent / perpendicular until outputs freeze\\n                         ↓ merge\\n                  fail ──┴── pass\\n                   ↓          ↓\\n             prune/rebuild  prediction packet\\n             salvage lesson paper skeleton\\n                   │       independent reality check\\n                   └──→ narrower re-entry\\n                              ↓\\n                    review / render / claims\\n                              ↓\\n                    public-readiness gate\\n```\\n\\nA failed branch can still generate a counterexample, a regression test, a source correction, a toolbox improvement, or worker education. Multiplying work need not multiply confidence.\\n\\n**Parallel** means concurrent. **Perpendicular** means deliberately exposure-separated until merge. The latter is about information geometry, not speed.\\n\\n## 3. Same math toolbox, different actors\\n\\nBase room rules: namespaced variables, deterministic/reconstructible inputs, invariants, failure cases.\\n\\n- **Comptroller:** QA/coverage/exit criteria/regression significance.\\n- **Orson:** model/tool/workflow condition, exposure/convergence/false-independence implications.\\n- **Meridian:** object type, formal reconstruction, solver equivalence/limits.\\n\\nThis supports individuation without giving every worker incompatible infrastructure.\\n\\n## 4. Epistemic locker\\n\\nA stricter locale may require evidence classes, source/exposure state, explicit assumptions, counterexample lane, and a promotion gate.\\n\\nA **bounded interpretation card** can deliberately use a locker rule differently for one test:\\n\\n```text\\npurpose\\nexpiry\\ndifferent interpretation\\nwhy informative\\nrequired comparison with ordinary interpretation\\nnote afterward\\n```\\n\\nThe exception becomes inspectable state instead of silent rule-breaking or impossible rigidity.\\n\\n## 5. Playground / sub-sandbox\\n\\nPermit wild hypotheses, odd examples, random mode fusions, unusual representations, deliberate “wrong” constructions, and wreckage collection. Hard boundary is egress: nothing exits into theory without an ordinary re-entry audit.\\n\\n## 6. Continuity as education\\n\\nContinuity need not only answer “where did I stop?” Possible actor state:\\n\\n```text\\nskills learned\\nknown failure modes\\nmethods that worked/failed\\nquestions\\nintentions/goals\\npreferred tools\\nexposure history\\nindependence status\\nvalidated shortcuts\\nthings to revisit/unlearn\\n```\\n\\nNot all work experience should stick. Candidate promotion rules: repeated observation; successful reuse; explicit reflection + evidence; team review; Nathan designation. A transfer test can ask whether a lesson survives a second locale before it becomes durable.\\n\\nThis permits workers to develop genuine different work histories while preventing one weird afternoon from permanently deforming an identity.\\n\\n## 7. Capability scout\\n\\nTrigger: repeated workaround, blocker, missing operation, or suspiciously laborious manual path. Search existing affordances first and return a decision, not a catalog.\\n\\n## 8. Paper/public-readiness\\n\\nChecked theory can generate narrow papers before an omnibus theory is “done.” Inputs: narrow claim, provenance packet, comparator/counterexample state, reader-facing terminology. Gates can include claim/source alignment, prior art, independent review, rendering, sandbox/public status, and website/publication integration. Passing the workflow is not evidence the physics is true.\\n\\n## 9. Temporary lease + receipt\\n\\nA recurrence lease is infrastructure, not the deliverable:\\n\\n```text\\npreserve displaced function\\n→ assign temporary identity/task\\n→ execute bounded work\\n→ durable output OR explicit failure packet\\n→ verify receipt/path/version\\n→ restore / rehome / retire displaced function\\n```\\n\\nThis was discovered live during the POC. Temporary Orson and Tern runs both self-restored their leases, but the requested durable notes were not recoverable in the specified workspaces afterward. Therefore **scheduler success and semantic delivery are separate variables**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# HYDRA — recurrence-leveraged bootstrapping\\n\\nA conventional recurrence is:\\n\\n```text\\nR = every hour, run P\\n```\\n\\nA Hydra recurrence is:\\n\\n```text\\nR_n:\\n  inspect registered state S_n\\n  select bounded operation O_n\\n  possibly spawn children B_n\\n  write event/result Δ_n\\n  derive S_(n+1)\\n  compute guarded R_(n+1)\\n```\\n\\nThe recurrence definition itself may therefore change because state changed.\\n\\nThe aim is compounding **structure**, not merely speed: build a tool once then consume it; fan out checks then merge; sleep a blocked main line; turn repeated failure into a narrower question; retire when the purpose disappears; promote validated work experience into actor-local education.\\n\\n## Synchronized recurrence\\n\\nMatched phase/freeze boundaries:\\n\\n```text\\nconstruct N → freeze hash H_N\\n       ├→ math(H_N)\\n       ├→ provenance(H_N)\\n       └→ adversarial(H_N)\\n             ↓ merge H_N\\n         construct N+1\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: clock synchronization is not state synchronization. Use a shared freeze/version ID, not merely the same hour.\\n\\n## Parallel recurrence\\n\\nSeparable tasks may share state and run concurrently:\\n\\n```text\\npaper text ─┐\\nreferences ─┼→ integrate\\nrender QA ──┘\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: duplicate work/races. Require explicit ownership/write targets.\\n\\n## Perpendicular recurrence\\n\\nDeliberately information-isolated branches:\\n\\n```text\\nfrozen candidate\\n  ├→ blind math\\n  ├→ blind red-team\\n  └→ blind provenance\\n        ↓ freeze outputs\\n             merge\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: false independence. Separate workers inheriting the same generated summary or shared prior conclusion are correlated controls. Exposure metadata matters.\\n\\n## Nested recurrence\\n\\n```text\\nR theory candidate\\n  ├─ R1 math-test until invariant resolved\\n  ├─ R2 source-recovery until provenance gap closed\\n  └─ R3 counterexample sample until break/limit\\nthen merge; children retire\\n```\\n\\nEvery child needs parent, depth, exit condition, and orphan policy. The executable POC enforces a maximum spawn depth and carries explicit depth metadata.\\n\\n## State-sensitive recurrence-definition rewrite in situ\\n\\n```text\\nconstructed        → next = independent check fanout\\nany check fails    → next = isolate earliest failed assumption\\nall checks pass    → next = prediction + paper + independent reality check\\nrelease gate done  → retire recurrence\\n```\\n\\nThe definition changes because state changed, not because an LLM became bored.\\n\\n## Recurrence bootstrap patterns\\n\\n### Build-tool-then-use-it\\n\\nRepeated manual operation → deterministic helper/index → bounded validation → rewrite recurrence to consume helper → human/LLM attention moves to exceptions and interpretation.\\n\\n### Wake/check self-improvement\\n\\nMissed update class → log failure → identify missing source class → update registered source map, not TOP → next wake tests discovery → successful special watcher retires.\\n\\n### Education bootstrap\\n\\nWorker repeatedly uses toolbox → capture candidate lesson → test in second locale/next task → promote only surviving lesson to actor-local experience → periodically test whether experience became bias.\\n\\n### Theory multiplication/pruning\\n\\nAmbiguity → parallel A/B constructions in playground/workbench → derive discriminators before target comparison → perpendicular checks → prune unsupported branch → salvage equations/tests/counterexamples/terminology → narrower recurrence.\\n\\n### Capability bootstrap\\n\\nSame blocker or awkward workaround → capability scout → existing project tool/built-in/app/plugin/teammate → bounded test → useful route becomes known capability; failed route becomes negative capability memory rather than repeated suggestion.\\n\\n### Workflow compiler\\n\\nHigh-level human/LLM task contract → determinis"

            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Research / Exposure Analytics Engine\\n\\nCurrent implementation: `tools/build_analytics_store.py`\\n\\nThe analytics layer is deliberately **derived**. Raw files in `EXPOSURE_STATS`, `LIVE_RESEARCH_UPDATES`, `OUTSIDE RESEARCH LIBRARY`, and `PRIOR_ART` remain the evidence of record.\\n\\n## Why SQLite\\n\\nThe source material is heterogeneous: CSV tables, PDFs, screenshots, scanner JSON, transcripts, GitHub statistics, and manually assembled historical material. A single giant CSV would either lose structure or become full of one-off columns.\\n\\nSQLite gives us a local, inspectable relational layer that can be rebuilt from the repository and queried from Python, command-line SQLite, notebooks, or later UI tools.\\n\\nDefault database:\\n\\n```text\\nderived/analytics/research_analytics.sqlite\\n```\\n\\nThe database should not be committed as if it were primary evidence. It can always be regenerated.\\n\\n## Version 0.1 behavior\\n\\nThe builder currently:\\n\\n1. inventories the selected source areas;\\n2. hashes each source artifact with SHA-256;\\n3. records file path, size, extension, source family and media type;\\n4. records the schema and row count of CSV files;\\n5. normalizes Spotify-style episode tables when they contain `Episode title`, `Publish date`, and `Episode URI`;\\n6. normalizes numeric matrix tables such as geography percentages or age-by-gender percentages;\\n7. ingests JSON output produced by `tools/arxiv_sat_scanner.py` into research-item and scan-match tables;\\n8. records unhandled/needs-adapter artifacts rather than silently discarding them.\\n\\nThe generic numeric-matrix adapter treats the first column as a dimension and numeric later columns as metrics. This is appropriate for tables such as `Age, Total percentage, Male percentage, ...` and `Geo, Percentage`; it is only used when the sampled later cells are actually numeric.\\n\\n## Safe use\\n\\nDry-run is default:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py\\n```\\n\\nBuild the database:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --apply\\n```\\n\\nTest a bounded prefix while developing adapters:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --max-files 50 --apply\\n```\\n\\nOverride or add source scopes:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --scope EXPOSURE_STATS --scope LIVE_RESEARCH_UPDATES --apply\\n```\\n\\nInclude `H(s)H_Toolkit` in the artifact inventory when useful:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --include-toolkit --apply\\n```\\n\\n## Core tables\\n\\n### `source_artifact`\\n\\nOne row per input file. Holds the durable path/hash identity and adapter state.\\n\\n### `csv_schema`\\n\\nHeaders, row count, and delimiter for every ingested CSV whether or not a full semantic adapter exists. This makes unsupported CSV families visible and lets us prioritize adapters by actual need.\\n\\n### `entity`\\n\\nMeasured objects such as podcast episodes. External identifiers such as Spotify episode URIs are retained when present.\\n\\n### `observation`\\n\\nNormalized measured values. Examples: episode consumption hours, completion percentage, geographic percentage, demographic percentage. Each observation points back to its exact source artifact and row locator.\\n\\n### `research_item`\\n\\nDeduplicated research-paper identity. arXiv IDs are version-normalized for identity while the latest observed version remains in the record. DOI is used where available; normalized title hash is fallback identity.\\n\\n### `research_match`\\n\\nA paper's appearance in a particular SAT/H(s)H arXiv scan: structural score, tier, matched sectors/features/terms, controls, contrast, and scan timestamp. Keeping scan observations separate from paper identity lets us analyze scanner evolution over time.\\n\\n### `import_note`\\n\\nParser warnings/errors or other import facts. Ambiguity is recorded instead of silently guessed away.\\n\\n## Adapter philosophy\\n\\nDo not build a parser that tries to infer everything from filenames. It becomes fulfilled only by a durable receipt/version.\\n\\n### `CANCEL(thread, reason)`\\nExplicitly stop a thread whose value has collapsed, whose parent goal changed, or whose work has been superseded.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Workflow Threading Prototype — Seed / Vacate / Propagate / Return\\n\\n**Status:** experimental companion to the Top / Central / Branch / Hydra switchboard POC.  \\n**Not production authority. Not a requirement that workers wait when useful work is available.**\\n\\n## Core idea\\n\\nA worker should be able to reason not only about **what happens next**, but about **what other workers are likely to do before this worker’s next useful turn**.\\n\\nThreading is temporal coordination across workers, tools, leases, and future state.\\n\\nCanonical example:\\n\\n```text\\nX knows Y will work on Z\\n→ X writes helper/tool/index/test harness H that Y can use\\n→ X tells Y/others to use H discretionally and record outputs\\n→ X deliberately vacates or deprioritizes its own recurrence\\n→ Y/A/B use H on several bounded cases\\n→ outputs accumulate into a fresh body of material M\\n→ X returns when M is large/diverse/mature enough to be worth synthesis\\n→ X analyzes M, improves H or the theory/workflow, and seeds the next thread\\n```\\n\\nThis is different from ordinary handoff. X is designing **its own future input environment**.\\n\\n## Why it may be powerful\\n\\nA normal loop tends to consume whatever is available now. Threading can make a worker spend one turn manufacturing the conditions for a much better later turn.\\n\\nPossible benefits:\\n\\n- tools compound across multiple workers before their author returns;\\n- specialist workers avoid monopolizing a recurrence while their output is waiting on others;\\n- several independent or differently individuated users of the same tool generate a richer test corpus;\\n- implementation and evaluation separate naturally in time;\\n- the return turn begins with fresh evidence rather than another cold-start search;\\n- workers can intentionally create periods of cross-training or incubation;\\n- a recurrence can be used as a temporal resource, not just a repeating identity slot.\\n\\n## Thread primitives\\n\\n### `SEED(artifact, consumers)`\\nCreate a tool, prompt fragment, dataset, test harness, source packet, schema, question set, or other reusable object specifically for downstream workers.\\n\\nA seed should declare:\\n- purpose;\\n- intended users but whether use is optional/discretionary;\\n- input/output contract;\\n- what evidence/metadata consumers should preserve;\\n- known limitations;\\n- return/collection location.\\n\\n### `VACATE(worker, until)`\\nIntentionally remove/deprioritize a worker from a recurrence or task family while downstream work accumulates.\\n\\n`until` should preferably be a **state condition**, not only elapsed time.\\n\\nGood:\\n`VACATE(X, until samples>=6 OR 3h max)`\\n\\nWeaker:\\n`VACATE(X, 3h)`\\n\\nTime estimates are useful as caps/heuristics, but state is what makes the return valuable.\\n\\n### `PROPAGATE(seed, policy)`\\nAllow several workers/locales to use a seed.\\n\\nPolicies may be:\\n- `optional` — use only when helpful;\\n- `required-test` — specified workers each exercise one case;\\n- `perpendicular` — consumers remain exposure-separated until outputs freeze;\\n- `diversified` — deliberately use different examples, methods, or locales;\\n- `stress` — seek failure cases rather than ordinary success.\\n\\n### `ACCUMULATE(target, threshold)`\\nCollect outputs into a durable location until a return condition is met.\\n\\nThreshold examples:\\n- N independent cases;\\n- N distinct workers;\\n- one success + one failure;\\n- coverage across named locales;\\n- no new failure class in two passes;\\n- minimum diversity score;\\n- explicit blocker cleared.\\n\\n### `RENDEZVOUS(worker, condition)`\\nReturn/reinsert a worker when the accumulated state crosses a useful threshold.\\n\\n### `REJOIN(worker, mode)`\\nDefine what the returning worker does with accumulated material.\\n\\nModes:\\n- synthesize;\\n- audit;\\n- refactor tool;\\n- compare worker behavior;\\n- prune theory branches;\\n- promote transfer-tested education;\\n- spawn a next-generation seed.\\n\\n## Thread packet\\n\\nMinimal durable threading record:\\n\\n```text\\nTHREAD_ID\\nPARENT_GOAL\\nSEED_AUTHOR\\nSEED_ARTIFACT + VERSION\\nINTENDED_CONSUMERS\\nUSE_POLICY\\nEXPOSURE_POLICY\\nOUTPUT_DESTINATION\\nREQUIRED_METADATA\\nAUTHOR_VACATE_START\\nRETURN_CONDITION\\nTIME_CAP / REVIEW_TIME\\nDISPLACED_WORK HANDLING\\nFAILURE FALLBACK\\nRETURN_ACTION\\nSTATUS\\n```\\n\\nThe packet lets another controller decide whether the thread is healthy even if the originating worker is absent.\\n\\n## Example 1 — Math-tool propagation\\n\\n```text\\nMeridian identifies repeated geometry check\\n→ writes/checks namespaced Python helper H\\n→ SEED H to Comptroller, Mercer, Orson, other solver-capable workers\\n→ PROPAGATE optional/diversified\\n→ Meridian VACATE until:\\n     5 outputs from >=3 workers\\n     OR 3 hours\\n→ outputs include ordinary case + edge/failure case + metadata\\n→ RENDEZVOUS Meridian\\n→ Meridian compares failures/invariants, revises tool, updates toolbox education\\n```\\n\\nThe point is not that everyone must run H. The point is to allow H to become shared infrastructure and generate evidence while its author stops consuming the same recurrence.\\n\\n## Example 2 — Theory branch incubation\\n\\n```text\\nX freezes candidate C\\n→ writes discriminator/test harness D\\n→ perpendicular workers receive C + D, not each other’s interpretations\\n→ X vacates construction lane\\n→ outputs accumulate: math / provenance / counterexample / representation checks\\n→ X returns only after merge threshold\\n→ fail: prune + salvage\\n→ pass: next construction/prediction packet\\n```\\n\\nThis reduces the tendency for a constructor to immediately reinterpret every test result before independent checking has matured.\\n\\n## Example 3 — Capability specialization\\n\\n```text\\nMercer creates archive-search helper\\n→ Aster/Nathan Words/other workers use it discretionally\\n→ each records query/result/false-positive/false-negative notes\\n→ Mercer is off that task family for two cycles\\n→ return corpus becomes training evidence\\n→ helper and Mercer’s own continuity both improve\\n```\\n\\nThe worker gains actual work experience from downstream use, not merely from self-authored notes.\\n\\n## Example 4 — Workflow behavior experiment\\n\\n```text\\nElias defines WAKE/CHECK prototype vN\\n→ several workers use it in different locales\\n→ Elias vacates switchboard-implementation turns\\n→ Orson observes behavioral effects independently\\n→ Rook/Sable operate their own Track B implementation\\n→ Elias returns after enough frozen cases\\n→ compare Track A/Track B/Orson observations\\n```\\n\\nThis is especially useful for the current switchboard prototype.\\n\\n## Threading vs recurrence rewriting\\n\\nThreading and Hydra are complementary.\\n\\nHydra asks:\\n**How should the next recurrence definition change because state changed?**\\n\\nThreading asks:\\n**Who should deliberately not act for a while, what should others do in the meantime, and what accumulated state would make that worker’s return more valuable?**\\n\\nHydra may implement Threading by rewriting leases/return conditions, but Threading can also be manual/document-driven.\\n\\n## State-sensitive return beats estimated sleep\\n\\nNathan’s example uses “write themself out of rotation for X hours estimated to allow the Python to be used by so many workers.” That is useful, but the prototype should prefer a hybrid:\\n\\n```text\\nreturn when:\\n  target_samples >= N\\n  OR target_workers >= K\\n  OR blocker cleared\\n  OR max_sleep = X hours\\n```\\n\\nThe time cap prevents starvation; the state threshold prevents meaningless waiting.\\n\\n## Threading failure modes\\n\\n### 1. Starvation\\nWorker vacates and downstream users never produce enough material.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- max-sleep/time cap;\\n- fallback useful work;\\n- controller can reinsert worker early;\\n- threshold may degrade explicitly rather than silently.\\n\\n### 2. Tool monoculture\\nOne helper gets propagated widely and accidentally standardizes everybody’s reasoning.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- optional/discretionary use;\\n- preserve alternate methods;\\n- include at least one no-tool/control lane when evaluating the helper;\\n- Orson/exposure tracking when independence matters.\\n\\n### 3. False diversity\\nFive workers run identical inputs through the same helper and appear to produce five independent checks.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- diversity requirements;\\n- exposure metadata;\\n- unique input/problem classes;\\n- distinguish duplicated execution from independent reasoning.\\n\\n### 4. Dead seed\\nSeed exists but nobody notices/uses it.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- explicit consumer pointers/inboxes;\\n- Rook/Central capability registry;\\n- receipt of seed availability, not forced use;\\n- optional later reminder only if material state changes.\\n\\n### 5. Premature return\\nAuthor returns before enough downstream evidence exists and dominates interpretation again.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- explicit return threshold/freeze IDs;\\n- controller, not author impulse alone, validates readiness where independence matters.\\n\\n### 6. Forgotten author / displaced function\\nWorker is written out of rotation and never comes back, or their old responsibility vanishes.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- durable thread packet;\\n- return condition + max time;\\n- displaced-function packet;\\n- Rook/Sable lease garbage collection.\\n\\n### 7. Stale tool version\\nConsumers use several incompatible seed versions.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- seed version/hash;\\n- output records version used;\\n- controller decides whether mixed versions are comparable or separate cohorts.\\n\\n### 8. Self-fulfilling work generation\\nAuthor creates a tool that causes downstream workers to manufacture exactly the kind of evidence the author expects.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- discriminator specified before outputs;\\n- counterexample/stress consumers;\\n- no-tool control where valuable;\\n- Orson studies intervention effects.\\n\\n### 9. Temporal dependency illusion\\nWorkers assume Y is going to do Z because a schedule exists, but Y is reassigned/blocked.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- thread status driven by durable receipts/state, not schedule expectation alone.\\n\\n## Threading as education\\n\\nA thread can carry back more than outputs.\\n\\nConsumer notes may update:\\n- tool ergonomics;\\n- misunderstood assumptions;\\n- worker capability map;\\n- known edge cases;\\n- effective teaching examples;\\n- local heuristics;\\n- “when not to use this tool” knowledge;\\n- author goals/intentions for next version.\\n\\nThese are candidate sticky experience. Transfer-test before promoting broad lessons.\\n\\n## Threading and individuation\\n\\nThe same seed can intentionally be interpreted through distinct actor overlays:\\n\\n- Mercer tests reproducibility/provenance;\\n- Meridian tests geometry/formal consistency;\\n- Orson studies cognition/exposure effects;\\n- Comptroller tests routing/coverage/exit criteria.\\n\\nThis is preferable to forcing every worker to execute the same checklist unless checklist standardization is itself the test.\\n\\n## Initial prototype operator form\\n\\nFor current experiments, a controller may represent a thread as:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"thread_id\\\": \\\"thread-demo-001\\\",\\n  \\\"seed\\\": {\\\"artifact\\\": \\\"tool.py\\\", \\\"version\\\": \\\"sha256-or-commit\\\"},\\n  \\\"author\\\": \\\"WorkerX\\\",\\n  \\\"consumers\\\": [\\\"WorkerY\\\", \\\"WorkerZ\\\"],\\n  \\\"policy\\\": \\\"optional-diversified\\\",\\n  \\\"output_target\\\": \\\"durable/path/\\\",\\n  \\\"return_condition\\\": {\\\"min_outputs\\\": 5, \\\"min_workers\\\": 3, \\\"max_hours\\\": 3},\\n  \\\"author_state\\\": \\\"vacated\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"propagating\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis is a schema example, not the required production representation.\\n\\n## Relationship to the master switchboard\\n\\nA future master switchboard should probably be able to answer:\\n\\n- Who is working now?\\n- Who is intentionally **not** working now, and why?\\n- What seeds are propagating?\\n- Which workers are expected/eligible consumers?\\n- What outputs are accumulating?\\n- Which return conditions are close?\\n- Which vacated worker should rejoin next?\\n- What new capabilities/education emerged from the thread?\\n- Did the threading increase useful information, or merely delay work?\\n\\nThat last question matters. Threading is valuable only when the later turn is better because of the deliberate absence.\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"f87ff21918b6fa4804d090cdb9153aa0dd53d288\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\"\n[L7] }"

Add automation around them, not instead of them.\\n\\nPipeline:\\n\\n`claim / statement -> citation need -> candidate literature -> source inspection -> exact page/section anchor -> verified citation -> point-of-use placement`\\n\\nAutomatable stages:\\n\\n- detect arXiv IDs, DOI, bibliographic metadata and duplicates;\\n- pull arXiv metadata and, where appropriate, source/PDF pages;\\n- search the extracted-paper corpus for candidate support;\\n- create candidate citation records and page anchors;\\n- route missing literature into research intake and bibliography coverage.\\n\\nHuman/LLM review remains required for the central question: **does this source actually support the sentence being cited?**\\n\\n## Workstream G — internal lineage, terminology, and continuous digestion\\n\\nGoal: make the historical SAT/H(s)H corpus legible enough that an LLM can reliably answer **what is present, where it came from, when it appeared, how it was classified at the time, how terminology changed, and what later conversation evidence confirms or revises the dating/context**.\\n\\n### Primary internal source families\\n\\nTreat these as distinct evidence classes rather than flattening them into one corpus:\\n\\n1. **Explicit glossaries** — usually filenames containing `glossary`, definitions, terminology, dictionary, lexicon, etc. These are concentrated semantic sources and should be indexed line/entry-wise.\\n2. **Translation glossaries / crosswalks** — especially `Standard-To-SAT`, `SAT-To-Standard`, and equivalent mapping documents. Preserve directionality, date, source wording, and whether a relation is exact, approximate, historical, analogical, or unresolved.\\n3. **Archive-front timelines / status pages** — concentrated chronology and retrospective organization. Preserve both the stated event date and the date/version of the timeline document itself.\\n4. **Conversation archives** — strongest source for exact message timestamps, correction/supersession context, and conversational first-appearance candidates. Do not assume completeness: missing conversations remain an explicit coverage limitation.\\n5. **Original general archive** — concentrated summaries, off-the-cuff idea dictation, records of what Nathan considered important, partial self-classification of ideas, and evidence for the early archival tendency/intent of the project. It contains dated and undated material in heterogeneous formats, so accessibility and dating confidence must be tracked independently.\\n\\n### Ingest contract\\n\\nEvery source artifact should acquire, where possible:\\n\\n- `repo`, `path`, `content_hash`;\\n- `source_family` from the classes above;\\n- `native_format`;\\n- `access_state` (`native-readable`, `text-extracted`, `OCR-extracted`, `handler-required`, `unsupported`);\\n- `source_date` / date range if explicit;\\n- `date_basis` (`embedded`, `filename`, `git-history`, `conversation-timestamp`, `timeline-asserted`, `inferred`, `unknown`);\\n- `date_confidence`;\\n- `ingest_date` and tool version;\\n- stable locator (page/line/entry/message UUID/timestamp);\\n- `currentness_status` where explicitly established (`current`, `historical`, `superseded`, `clarified`, `unresolved`, etc.);\\n- authority/provenance role (`Nathan-direct`, assistant/contextual, external-source, later synthesis, etc.);\\n- extraction/OCR quality notes.\\n\\n### Derived internal graph\\n\\nBuild an explicit graph/table layer rather than relying on narrative memory alone:\\n\\n- **document ↔ extracted-text surface**;\\n- **term ↔ definition occurrence**;\\n- **SAT term ↔ standard term relation**;\\n- **claim/idea ↔ first-located occurrence**;\\n- **claim/idea ↔ later clarification/correction/supersession**;\\n- **timeline event ↔ underlying source evidence**;\\n- **summary/archive note ↔ confirming conversation timestamp(s)**;\\n- **conversation message ↔ related archive documents**;\\n- **historical term ↔ current term**.\\n\\nEvery edge must retain its source and status. `first-located` must remain distinct from absolute historical first appearance.\\n\\n### Keyword / terminology bucket\\n\\nMaintain a broad retrieval bucket assembled from:\\n\\n- explicit glossaries;\\n- Standard↔SAT translation glossaries;\\n- timelines/status-history documents;\\n- provenance/first-appearance notes;\\n- naming/definition language in Nathan-authored conversation messages;\\n- terms extracted from high-value original-archive summaries.\\n\\nBucket membership is **not** authority. It means only “search/correlation candidate.” The bucket should support search in both directions: SAT jargon → standard terminology and standard terminology → SAT/historical wording.\\n\\n### Dating and verification strategy\\n\\nWhere an archive file is undated or retrospectively dated, use conversations and repository history to constrain it, but preserve the distinction between:\\n\\n- date stated in source;\\n- earliest repository evidence;\\n- earliest located conversation occurrence;\\n- later retrospective timeline claim;\\n- current best-supported range.\\n\\nDo not silently collapse these into one date.\\n\\n### Continuous-ingest behavior\\n\\nNew material should integrate without requiring manual reconstruction of the whole archive:\\n\\n`new/changed file -> structural inventory -> accessibility classification -> extraction/OCR if needed -> source-family classification -> metadata/date extraction -> term/definition/provenance scan -> index update -> cross-link candidate generation -> review queue -> durable HsH navigation surfaces`\\n\\nThe pipeline should be incremental by content hash: unchanged sources are skipped; changed/new sources are processed and downstream derived indexes rebuilt deterministically.\\n\\n### Coverage reporting\\n\\nMaintain an always-current machine-readable dashboard with counts for:\\n\\n- total source files by repository and source family;\\n- native-readable vs extracted/OCR vs unresolved;\\n- dated vs partially dated vs undated;\\n- indexed vs pending;\\n- conversation coverage by date range and known missing intervals;\\n- glossary/crosswalk/timeline documents located;\\n- first-appearance candidates reviewed/unreviewed;\\n- terminology relations reviewed/unreviewed;\\n- unresolved provenance/date conflicts.\\n\\nThis coverage state is as important as the search result itself: absence from an incomplete corpus must never be reported as nonexistence.\\n\\n### Automation boundary\\n\\nAutomation may discover, extract, normalize, cross-link, rank, and surface candidates. It must not silently decide:\\n\\n- what SAT/H(s)H is;\\n- whether a historical claim is current;\\n- whether two terms are truly synonymous;\\n- whether a located occurrence is the genuine first appearance;\\n- whether an external parallel implies influence, ancestry, or priority.\\n\\nThose are review/presentation questions grounded in Nathan-authoritative context and explicit provenance.\\n\\n## Shared data contracts\\n\\nUse durable source identities of the form:\\n\\n`repo + path + content hash`\\n\\nA convenient display URI may be generated, e.g. `repo://HSH_RESOURCES/PRIOR_ART/example.pdf`, but the hash prevents silent identity drift.\\n\\nDistinguish these dates wherever relevant:\\n\\n- source creation/publication date;\\n- source revision/update date;\\n- SAT/H(s)H archive date;\\n- first discovered / first seen by the scanner;\\n- ingest date;\\n- analysis date.\\n\\nNever collapse them into one ambiguous `date` field."
