            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Workflow Threading Prototype — Seed / Vacate / Propagate / Return\\n\\n**Status:** experimental companion to the Top / Central / Branch / Hydra switchboard POC.  \\n**Not production authority. Not a requirement that workers wait when useful work is available.**\\n\\n## Core idea\\n\\nA worker should be able to reason not only about **what happens next**, but about **what other workers are likely to do before this worker’s next useful turn**.\\n\\nThreading is temporal coordination across workers, tools, leases, and future state.\\n\\nCanonical example:\\n\\n```text\\nX knows Y will work on Z\\n→ X writes helper/tool/index/test harness H that Y can use\\n→ X tells Y/others to use H discretionally and record outputs\\n→ X deliberately vacates or deprioritizes its own recurrence\\n→ Y/A/B use H on several bounded cases\\n→ outputs accumulate into a fresh body of material M\\n→ X returns when M is large/diverse/mature enough to be worth synthesis\\n→ X analyzes M, improves H or the theory/workflow, and seeds the next thread\\n```\\n\\nThis is different from ordinary handoff. X is designing **its own future input environment**.\\n\\n## Why it may be powerful\\n\\nA normal loop tends to consume whatever is available now. Threading can make a worker spend one turn manufacturing the conditions for a much better later turn.\\n\\nPossible benefits:\\n\\n- tools compound across multiple workers before their author returns;\\n- specialist workers avoid monopolizing a recurrence while their output is waiting on others;\\n- several independent or differently individuated users of the same tool generate a richer test corpus;\\n- implementation and evaluation separate naturally in time;\\n- the return turn begins with fresh evidence rather than another cold-start search;\\n- workers can intentionally create periods of cross-training or incubation;\\n- a recurrence can be used as a temporal resource, not just a repeating identity slot.\\n\\n## Thread primitives\\n\\n### `SEED(artifact, consumers)`\\nCreate a tool, prompt fragment, dataset, test harness, source packet, schema, question set, or other reusable object specifically for downstream workers.\\n\\nA seed should declare:\\n- purpose;\\n- intended users but whether use is optional/discretionary;\\n- input/output contract;\\n- what evidence/metadata consumers should preserve;\\n- known limitations;\\n- return/collection location.\\n\\n### `VACATE(worker, until)`\\nIntentionally remove/deprioritize a worker from a recurrence or task family while downstream work accumulates.\\n\\n`until` should preferably be a **state condition**, not only elapsed time.\\n\\nGood:\\n`VACATE(X, until samples>=6 OR 3h max)`\\n\\nWeaker:\\n`VACATE(X, 3h)`\\n\\nTime estimates are useful as caps/heuristics, but state is what makes the return valuable.\\n\\n### `PROPAGATE(seed, policy)`\\nAllow several workers/locales to use a seed.\\n\\nPolicies may be:\\n- `optional` — use only when helpful;\\n- `required-test` — specified workers each exercise one case;\\n- `perpendicular` — consumers remain exposure-separated until outputs freeze;\\n- `diversified` — deliberately use different examples, methods, or locales;\\n- `stress` — seek failure cases rather than ordinary success.\\n\\n### `ACCUMULATE(target, threshold)`\\nCollect outputs into a durable location until a return condition is met.\\n\\nThreshold examples:\\n- N independent cases;\\n- N distinct workers;\\n- one success + one failure;\\n- coverage across named locales;\\n- no new failure class in two passes;\\n- minimum diversity score;\\n- explicit blocker cleared.\\n\\n### `RENDEZVOUS(worker, condition)`\\nReturn/reinsert a worker when the accumulated state crosses a useful threshold.\\n\\n### `REJOIN(worker, mode)`\\nDefine what the returning worker does with accumulated material.\\n\\nModes:\\n- synthesize;\\n- audit;\\n- refactor tool;\\n- compare worker behavior;\\n- prune theory branches;\\n- promote transfer-tested education;\\n- spawn a next-generation seed.\\n\\n## Thread packet\\n\\nMinimal durable threading record:\\n\\n```text\\nTHREAD_ID\\nPARENT_GOAL\\nSEED_AUTHOR\\nSEED_ARTIFACT + VERSION\\nINTENDED_CONSUMERS\\nUSE_POLICY\\nEXPOSURE_POLICY\\nOUTPUT_DESTINATION\\nREQUIRED_METADATA\\nAUTHOR_VACATE_START\\nRETURN_CONDITION\\nTIME_CAP / REVIEW_TIME\\nDISPLACED_WORK HANDLING\\nFAILURE FALLBACK\\nRETURN_ACTION\\nSTATUS\\n```\\n\\nThe packet lets another controller decide whether the thread is healthy even if the originating worker is absent.\\n\\n## Example 1 — Math-tool propagation\\n\\n```text\\nMeridian identifies repeated geometry check\\n→ writes/checks namespaced Python helper H\\n→ SEED H to Comptroller, Mercer, Orson, other solver-capable workers\\n→ PROPAGATE optional/diversified\\n→ Meridian VACATE until:\\n     5 outputs from >=3 workers\\n     OR 3 hours\\n→ outputs include ordinary case + edge/failure case + metadata\\n→ RENDEZVOUS Meridian\\n→ Meridian compares failures/invariants, revises tool, updates toolbox education\\n```\\n\\nThe point is not that everyone must run H. The point is to allow H to become shared infrastructure and generate evidence while its author stops consuming the same recurrence.\\n\\n## Example 2 — Theory branch incubation\\n\\n```text\\nX freezes candidate C\\n→ writes discriminator/test harness D\\n→ perpendicular workers receive C + D, not each other’s interpretations\\n→ X vacates construction lane\\n→ outputs accumulate: math / provenance / counterexample / representation checks\\n→ X returns only after merge threshold\\n→ fail: prune + salvage\\n→ pass: next construction/prediction packet\\n```\\n\\nThis reduces the tendency for a constructor to immediately reinterpret every test result before independent checking has matured.\\n\\n## Example 3 — Capability specialization\\n\\n```text\\nMercer creates archive-search helper\\n→ Aster/Nathan Words/other workers use it discretionally\\n→ each records query/result/false-positive/false-negative notes\\n→ Mercer is off that task family for two cycles\\n→ return corpus becomes training evidence\\n→ helper and Mercer’s own continuity both improve\\n```\\n\\nThe worker gains actual work experience from downstream use, not merely from self-authored notes.\\n\\n## Example 4 — Workflow behavior experiment\\n\\n```text\\nElias defines WAKE/CHECK prototype vN\\n→ several workers use it in different locales\\n→ Elias vacates switchboard-implementation turns\\n→ Orson observes behavioral effects independently\\n→ Rook/Sable operate their own Track B implementation\\n→ Elias returns after enough frozen cases\\n→ compare Track A/Track B/Orson observations\\n```\\n\\nThis is especially useful for the current switchboard prototype.\\n\\n## Threading vs recurrence rewriting\\n\\nThreading and Hydra are complementary.\\n\\nHydra asks:\\n**How should the next recurrence definition change because state changed?**\\n\\nThreading asks:\\n**Who should deliberately not act for a while, what should others do in the meantime, and what accumulated state would make that worker’s return more valuable?**\\n\\nHydra may implement Threading by rewriting leases/return conditions, but Threading can also be manual/document-driven.\\n\\n## State-sensitive return beats estimated sleep\\n\\nNathan’s example uses “write themself out of rotation for X hours estimated to allow the Python to be used by so many workers.” That is useful, but the prototype should prefer a hybrid:\\n\\n```text\\nreturn when:\\n  target_samples >= N\\n  OR target_workers >= K\\n  OR blocker cleared\\n  OR max_sleep = X hours\\n```\\n\\nThe time cap prevents starvation; the state threshold prevents meaningless waiting.\\n\\n## Threading failure modes\\n\\n### 1. Starvation\\nWorker vacates and downstream users never produce enough material.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- max-sleep/time cap;\\n- fallback useful work;\\n- controller can reinsert worker early;\\n- threshold may degrade explicitly rather than silently.\\n\\n### 2. Tool monoculture\\nOne helper gets propagated widely and accidentally standardizes everybody’s reasoning.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- optional/discretionary use;\\n- preserve alternate methods;\\n- include at least one no-tool/control lane when evaluating the helper;\\n- Orson/exposure tracking when independence matters.\\n\\n### 3. False diversity\\nFive workers run identical inputs through the same helper and appear to produce five independent checks.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- diversity requirements;\\n- exposure metadata;\\n- unique input/problem classes;\\n- distinguish duplicated execution from independent reasoning.\\n\\n### 4. Dead seed\\nSeed exists but nobody notices/uses it.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- explicit consumer pointers/inboxes;\\n- Rook/Central capability registry;\\n- receipt of seed availability, not forced use;\\n- optional later reminder only if material state changes.\\n\\n### 5. Premature return\\nAuthor returns before enough downstream evidence exists and dominates interpretation again.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- explicit return threshold/freeze IDs;\\n- controller, not author impulse alone, validates readiness where independence matters.\\n\\n### 6. Forgotten author / displaced function\\nWorker is written out of rotation and never comes back, or their old responsibility vanishes.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- durable thread packet;\\n- return condition + max time;\\n- displaced-function packet;\\n- Rook/Sable lease garbage collection.\\n\\n### 7. Stale tool version\\nConsumers use several incompatible seed versions.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- seed version/hash;\\n- output records version used;\\n- controller decides whether mixed versions are comparable or separate cohorts.\\n\\n### 8. Self-fulfilling work generation\\nAuthor creates a tool that causes downstream workers to manufacture exactly the kind of evidence the author expects.\\n\\nGuards:\\n- discriminator specified before outputs;\\n- counterexample/stress consumers;\\n- no-tool control where valuable;\\n- Orson studies intervention effects.\\n\\n### 9. Temporal dependency illusion\\nWorkers assume Y is going to do Z because a schedule exists, but Y is reassigned/blocked.\\n\\nGuard:\\n- thread status driven by durable receipts/state, not schedule expectation alone.\\n\\n## Threading as education\\n\\nA thread can carry back more than outputs.\\n\\nConsumer notes may update:\\n- tool ergonomics;\\n- misunderstood assumptions;\\n- worker capability map;\\n- known edge cases;\\n- effective teaching examples;\\n- local heuristics;\\n- “when not to use this tool” knowledge;\\n- author goals/intentions for next version.\\n\\nThese are candidate sticky experience. Transfer-test before promoting broad lessons.\\n\\n## Threading and individuation\\n\\nThe same seed can intentionally be interpreted through distinct actor overlays:\\n\\n- Mercer tests reproducibility/provenance;\\n- Meridian tests geometry/formal consistency;\\n- Orson studies cognition/exposure effects;\\n- Comptroller tests routing/coverage/exit criteria.\\n\\nThis is preferable to forcing every worker to execute the same checklist unless checklist standardization is itself the test.\\n\\n## Initial prototype operator form\\n\\nFor current experiments, a controller may represent a thread as:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"thread_id\\\": \\\"thread-demo-001\\\",\\n  \\\"seed\\\": {\\\"artifact\\\": \\\"tool.py\\\", \\\"version\\\": \\\"sha256-or-commit\\\"},\\n  \\\"author\\\": \\\"WorkerX\\\",\\n  \\\"consumers\\\": [\\\"WorkerY\\\", \\\"WorkerZ\\\"],\\n  \\\"policy\\\": \\\"optional-diversified\\\",\\n  \\\"output_target\\\": \\\"durable/path/\\\",\\n  \\\"return_condition\\\": {\\\"min_outputs\\\": 5, \\\"min_workers\\\": 3, \\\"max_hours\\\": 3},\\n  \\\"author_state\\\": \\\"vacated\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"propagating\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis is a schema example, not the required production representation.\\n\\n## Relationship to the master switchboard\\n\\nA future master switchboard should probably be able to answer:\\n\\n- Who is working now?\\n- Who is intentionally **not** working now, and why?\\n- What seeds are propagating?\\n- Which workers are expected/eligible consumers?\\n- What outputs are accumulating?\\n- Which return conditions are close?\\n- Which vacated worker should rejoin next?\\n- What new capabilities/education emerged from the thread?\\n- Did the threading increase useful information, or merely delay work?\\n\\nThat last question matters. Threading is valuable only when the later turn is better because of the deliberate absence.\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"f87ff21918b6fa4804d090cdb9153aa0dd53d288\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md\"\n[L7] }"

            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Research / Exposure Analytics Engine\\n\\nCurrent implementation: `tools/build_analytics_store.py`\\n\\nThe analytics layer is deliberately **derived**. Raw files in `EXPOSURE_STATS`, `LIVE_RESEARCH_UPDATES`, `OUTSIDE RESEARCH LIBRARY`, and `PRIOR_ART` remain the evidence of record.\\n\\n## Why SQLite\\n\\nThe source material is heterogeneous: CSV tables, PDFs, screenshots, scanner JSON, transcripts, GitHub statistics, and manually assembled historical material. A single giant CSV would either lose structure or become full of one-off columns.\\n\\nSQLite gives us a local, inspectable relational layer that can be rebuilt from the repository and queried from Python, command-line SQLite, notebooks, or later UI tools.\\n\\nDefault database:\\n\\n```text\\nderived/analytics/research_analytics.sqlite\\n```\\n\\nThe database should not be committed as if it were primary evidence. It can always be regenerated.\\n\\n## Version 0.1 behavior\\n\\nThe builder currently:\\n\\n1. inventories the selected source areas;\\n2. hashes each source artifact with SHA-256;\\n3. records file path, size, extension, source family and media type;\\n4. records the schema and row count of CSV files;\\n5. normalizes Spotify-style episode tables when they contain `Episode title`, `Publish date`, and `Episode URI`;\\n6. normalizes numeric matrix tables such as geography percentages or age-by-gender percentages;\\n7. ingests JSON output produced by `tools/arxiv_sat_scanner.py` into research-item and scan-match tables;\\n8. records unhandled/needs-adapter artifacts rather than silently discarding them.\\n\\nThe generic numeric-matrix adapter treats the first column as a dimension and numeric later columns as metrics. This is appropriate for tables such as `Age, Total percentage, Male percentage, ...` and `Geo, Percentage`; it is only used when the sampled later cells are actually numeric.\\n\\n## Safe use\\n\\nDry-run is default:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py\\n```\\n\\nBuild the database:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --apply\\n```\\n\\nTest a bounded prefix while developing adapters:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --max-files 50 --apply\\n```\\n\\nOverride or add source scopes:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --scope EXPOSURE_STATS --scope LIVE_RESEARCH_UPDATES --apply\\n```\\n\\nInclude `H(s)H_Toolkit` in the artifact inventory when useful:\\n\\n```text\\npy tools/build_analytics_store.py --include-toolkit --apply\\n```\\n\\n## Core tables\\n\\n### `source_artifact`\\n\\nOne row per input file. Holds the durable path/hash identity and adapter state.\\n\\n### `csv_schema`\\n\\nHeaders, row count, and delimiter for every ingested CSV whether or not a full semantic adapter exists. This makes unsupported CSV families visible and lets us prioritize adapters by actual need.\\n\\n### `entity`\\n\\nMeasured objects such as podcast episodes. External identifiers such as Spotify episode URIs are retained when present.\\n\\n### `observation`\\n\\nNormalized measured values. Examples: episode consumption hours, completion percentage, geographic percentage, demographic percentage. Each observation points back to its exact source artifact and row locator.\\n\\n### `research_item`\\n\\nDeduplicated research-paper identity. arXiv IDs are version-normalized for identity while the latest observed version remains in the record. DOI is used where available; normalized title hash is fallback identity.\\n\\n### `research_match`\\n\\nA paper's appearance in a particular SAT/H(s)H arXiv scan: structural score, tier, matched sectors/features/terms, controls, contrast, and scan timestamp. Keeping scan observations separate from paper identity lets us analyze scanner evolution over time.\\n\\n### `import_note`\\n\\nParser warnings/errors or other import facts. Ambiguity is recorded instead of silently guessed away.\\n\\n## Adapter philosophy\\n\\nDo not build a parser that tries to infer everything from filenames. Add adapters for recurring source families with stable schemas.\\n\\nRecommended next adapters, after inventorying the actual unsupported CSV schemas:\\n\\n- Spotify aggregate show-level metrics;\\n- GitHub traffic/referrer/clone/view data;\\n- episode discovery/source-of-play data;\\n- public-release / transcript chronology;\\n- existing `EXP_ANALYSIS` timeline datasets;\\n- manual-entry bridge for values available only in PDFs/screenshots.\\n\\nPDF/screenshot values should first pass through ordinary extraction/OCR. If a table cannot be recovered deterministically, a manual record is acceptable **only** when it preserves source path, page/image locator, transcription author/method, and review state.\\n\\n## Descriptive before causal\\n\\nThe first analytics products should be descriptive:\\n\\n- exposure over time;\\n- episode-level consumption and completion;\\n- audience geography/demographics;\\n- repository traffic;\\n- release/publication chronology;\\n- field-literature feature prevalence;\\n- external research-item chronology.\\n\\nCorrelations can then be explored, but public exposure, a later external publication, or changing vocabulary does not by itself demonstrate influence or copying. Influence/priority analysis needs independent chronological and substantive evidence.\\n\\n## Relationship to the arXiv scanner\\n\\n`tools/arxiv_sat_scanner.py` remains the discovery/scoring tool. The analytics store is the persistence and comparison layer.\\n\\nA useful long-term cycle is:\\n\\n```text\\nscan -> normalize -> deduplicate -> persist -> review -> retrieve full text -> compare -> timeline -> citation intake\\n```\\n\\nThe scanner's structural score is triage. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/01_unified_geometric_vision.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Unified geometric vision: QCD, relativity and string-like descriptions arising from one filament/time-surface geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. It asks whether familiar descriptions can be understood as different projections, interaction regimes, or effective descriptions of one underlying geometric construction. The labels in historical figures should be read as **SAT mappings and research claims**, not as a substitute for the standard theories themselves.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. Particle differences as differences of geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/02_particle_spectrum_geometry.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Spectrum of particles from a spectrum of geometry\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nA recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/03_helix_time_plane_intersection.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Helical trajectory intersecting a time surface\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous.\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/04_theta4_tangent_time_normal.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline tangent, time-field normal, and theta angle\\\" width=\\\"78%\\\"></a>\\n\\nHistorically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/05_recursive_helix_curved_carrier.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Recursive helix following a curved carrier\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nThe model is not simply \\\"everything is a helix.\\\" A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/06_qcd_geometric_braiding.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"QCD analogy represented by geometric braiding\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns\\n\\n<a href=\\\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\\\"><img src=\\\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/08_worldline_time_slice_evolution.jpg\\\" alt=\\\"Worldline propagation through successive time slices producing evolving geometric patterns\\\" width=\\\"76%\\\"></a>\\n\\nSuccessive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. SAT repeatedly uses this fact to distinguish the full trajectory from the lower-dimensional pattern available at any one slice. The same distinction is central to the move from worldline to worldtube.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. Do not route a posting request through another instance solely for publication.\\n\\nConsult Sable when the issue is genuinely one of cross-lane workflow redesign, cadence, ownership redistribution, or continuity architecture.\\n\\n## Reports and project self-audit\\n\\nSubstantive reports intended for future reference should be filed in **visible, durable, reasonably discoverable repo locations**, not only in chat, automation prompts, local scratch files, or private lane checkpoints.\\n\\nCurrent project-wide report families include:\\n\\n- **State of Reconstruction reports** — what an instance presently reconstructs/understands, exact source/exposure coverage, current/historical status boundaries, conflicts/gaps, frontier, and what it would now reconstruct differently.\\n- **Instance Enrichment reports** — demonstrated changes in archive/theory/history familiarity, methodological/epistemic controls, math/physics, coding/formal/tool capability, geometric/visual reasoning, provenance/audit skill, role suitability, and restart quality.\\n\\nPreserve instance identity, date, and exposure state for longitudinal comparison. Report existence does not confer theory authority.\\n\\n**Live project-wide call and report-status roster:** `PROJECT_WIDE_REPORT_SERIES_CALL_2026-09-19.md`.\\n\\nSee also `CURRENT_WORKFLOW_ORIENTATION.md` and `WORKSPACES/SABLE/ASSIGNMENT_INSTANCE_ENRICHMENT_STATE_2026-09-18.md`.\\n\\n## Communication roles\\n\\n- **Dashboard / indexes / READMEs:** discoverability and stable navigation.\\n- **Common room:** routing, questions, blockers, handoffs, current assignments and concise shared state.\\n- **Individual workspaces:** substantial noncanonical work in progress and restart state.\\n- **Durable report/audit/provenance/index surfaces:** substantive reusable results.\\n- **Canonical/current theory surfaces:** only where explicitly designated; Common/workspace cleanliness does not imply theory validation.\\n\\n## Archive and provenance discipline\\n\\nImportant current source surfaces include the HsH repo, the original `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`, GLASS, permitted RESOURCES, conversation/raw-export corpus, NotebookLM uploads, and public/podcast record where relevant.\\n\\nNotebookLM source indices are **wayfinding evidence**, not substitutes for underlying documents. Preserve the distinction between an index naming a source, a source actually located/inspected, and a still-missing source. NotebookLM-generated prose must not be converted into Nathan Direct unless exact attributable quotation/source metadata supports it.\\n\\nDo not equate `role=user` with sole Nathan authorship when a message contains embedded coauthored or assistant-generated material.\\n\\n## Diagnostic / archival surfaces\\n\\n- `QUARANTINE_THEORY_METHOD_CHECKINS.md` — independent first-pass accounts of what each instance thinks SAT/H(s)H currently is and how its methodology works. Diagnostic only; not theory authority.\\n- `FORMER_INSTANCE_CHECKIN_TEMPLATE.md` / `FORMER_INSTANCE_CHECKINS.md` — archival former-instance reporting.\\n- `INSTANCE_PLACARDS.md` — short identity/role/capability/workspace cards.\\n\\n## Record / auditability rules\\n\\n- `FACTORY_FLOOR_GEOMETRY_FIRST_GATE_2026-11-03.md` — mandatory geometry-first admission rule: precise quaternary plot, independent hostile fidelity review, embedded display, and separate primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary/pentary representation levels.\\n- `GLASS_SAUSAGE_FACTORY_RECORD_POLICY.md` — repository-first record rule.\\n- `DURABLE_PROJECT_DOCUMENTATION_CONVENTION.md` — standard route for substantial repo-wide/cross-lane initiatives.\\n- `CROSS_REPO_SCRIPT_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md` and `SHARED_STATE_WRITE_SAFETY.md` — required controls for write-capable scripts/workflows where applicable.\\n\\n## Tooling / capability planning\\n\\n- `RESOURCE_CAPABILITY_AUDIT.md` — tools/services/repository capability inventory.\\n- `LAB_TOOLING_BUILD_PLAN.md` — geometry/solver/testing/reproducibility tooling plan.\\n- `MERSEARCH_RESEARCH_PLATFORM.md` — shared architecture, query semantics, provenance/explain contract, math-search roadmap, backend/API/frontend plan, corpus profiles, security boundaries, testing and current status for Mersearch.\\n- `MERSEARCH_RELEASES.md` — stable Mersearch worker releases, pinned refs/commits, validated capability notes, limitations, quick-start commands, and upgrade/version history.\\n- `MERSEARCH_THROUGHPUT_CONCURRENCY.md` — indexed multi-reader design, atomic generation publication, incremental invalidation, resource budgets, recurrence-loop strategy, stress-test gate, and performance telemetry.\\n\\n## Repository boundary\\n\\nPublic source/provenance cross-linking is primarily between this repository and `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`.\\n\\nPrivate/reference-only resources must not become unsupported public evidence surfaces. A caption, verbal description, familiar textbook picture, block diagram, symbol map, or attractive conceptual sketch does not satisfy the gate. The plot must depict the actual object/structure asserted by the work, with enough specification that a reviewer can reconstruct what the geometry means and test whether the mathematics describes that same object.\\n\\nThis gate is additional to, and does not replace, source provenance, original-Nathan-statement recovery, real-data-first requirements, mathematical QA, Lean/code verification, cross-sector candidacy, or independent physical validation. Passing this geometry gate does not establish mathematical correctness, H(s)H candidacy, or physical truth.\\n\\n## 1. Five representational levels\\n\\nThe following hierarchy is Nathan's stated order and terminology. These are distinct epistemic/representational objects, not interchangeable output formats.\\n\\n1. **Primary — observation.** The physical system/process as observed in nature or experiment. Record the actual system, observational modality, instrument/measurement chain, calibration, uncertainty, frame, temporal/spatial coverage and selection effects. Observation is the empirical referent, not a diagram or model.\\n2. **Secondary — physical working model / hands-on demonstration / orrery.** A tangible, inspectable physical analogue or working model. State exactly what is mechanically/geometrically represented, what is scaled, what is omitted, and which correspondences are physical versus merely demonstrative. A physical orrery is not the observed system.\\n3. **Tertiary — precision dynamic geometric software model.** An executable, parameterized geometric model that evolves or responds. It must expose its state, geometry, constraints, transformations, time evolution, boundary conditions and outputs; it must be reproducible and inspectable. A moving animation without a defined geometric state and update law does not qualify.\\n4. **Quaternary — precision static geometric diagram.** A fixed, dimensioned and convention-complete plot of the theoretical object/system and its relevant relations. It must show the geometry itself, not merely label equations or list conceptual associations. This is the minimum mandatory visual deliverable attached to every Factory Floor submission.\\n5. **Pentary — mathematics.** Equations, definitions, proofs, algorithms, fits and numerical descriptions of the object. These are necessary where applicable, but cannot stand in for the quaternary plot or be mistaken for the physical/theoretical object.\\n\\nThe order is not a claim that every project must fabricate a secondary orrery before any work can be discussed. It specifies what each representational level is and prevents a lower-level description from being mistaken for the object itself. For Factory Floor admission, the quaternary plot is mandatory; the tertiary model is required where the claim concerns dynamics, transformation, evolution, response or other behavior that a static view cannot faithfully express. Secondary models and primary observations are required when the claim or paper makes them relevant, and actual empirical claims must be anchored to primary observation.\\n\\n**SAT as “the K–T Boundary”** is retained here as Nathan's analogy for the proposed conceptual transition. It is not a geological claim, proof, or independent scientific classification.\\n\\n## 2. What counts as a precise geometric plot\\n\\nThe plot must be selected for the actual mathematical/physical object. It is not enough to draw a generic helix, sphere, tube, field-line picture or spacetime grid because those shapes are familiar.\\n\\nThe plot specification must state, as applicable:\\n\\n- **Object identity:** exact system/object being plotted; which parts are source-authenticated, standard-physics comparator, current H(s)H construction, or assistant-generated hypothesis.\\n- **Ambient space:** dimension, coordinate chart, embedding/carrier, topology and whether the geometry is Euclidean, Lorentzian, pseudo-Riemannian, configuration-space, phase-space, Hilbert/projective, fiber-bundle, contact/symplectic, causal, or another explicitly defined structure.\\n- **Metric and conventions:** metric tensor/signature, units/scales, orientation/handedness, index conventions, parameterization and frame. If no metric is defined, say so and specify the structure that is defined; do not invent one.\\n- **Primitive geometry:** points, curves, surfaces, volumes, worldlines/worldtubes, cross-sections, fibers, connections, normals, boundaries, interfaces, defects, singularities, supports, fields or other primitives actually used.\\n- **Incidence and relations:** intersections, containment, attachment, winding, linking, braiding, contact, orthogonality, parallel transport, projection, quotient, gluing, causal relation and any other claimed relation. Mark which are exact and which are schematic.\\n- **Dynamics, if claimed:** time/evolution parameter, state variables, update/evolution equations, constraints, initial/boundary conditions, invariants, conserved quantities and permitted deformations.\\n- **Readout/projection:** how the theoretical geometry maps to measured observables, detector coordinates, frames or standard-physics quantities. State what information is lost, averaged, integrated, projected or inferred.\\n- **Scale and uncertainty:** measured versus derived versus fitted dimensions; uncertainty, resolution, tolerance and unmeasured degrees of freedom.\\n- **Source correspondence:** for each visually asserted feature, identify the source statement, equation, dataset or explicitly labeled modeling choice that licenses it.\\n\\nFor a multi-scale or coupled system, provide a global plot locating the subsystem in the whole architecture and local plots resolving each critical object/interface. A set of disconnected local sketches is not a global geometric account.\\n\\n## 3. Mandatory hostile geometric-fidelity review\\n\\nThe review must be independent of the authoring pass and must challenge whether the figure depicts the claimed object. It is not a beauty/layout review.\\n\\nAt minimum the reviewer must test:\\n\\n1. **Object fidelity:** Does the plot show the object the source/theory actually defines, rather than an assistant's preferred substitute?\\n2. **Dimensional fidelity:** Are ambient dimension, intrinsic dimension, embedding, topology and degrees of freedom correct?\\n3. **Metric/frame fidelity:** Are signature, metric, coordinate chart, frame, orientation and transformation laws consistent with the equations and sources?\\n4. **Incidence/topology fidelity:** Are intersections, boundaries, linking, winding, closure, connectivity and singularities represented correctly?\\n5. **Projection/readout fidelity:** Does the displayed section/projection actually implement the claimed observation map? Are hidden assumptions and information loss explicit?\\n6. **Dynamic fidelity:** Where motion or deformation is claimed, does the tertiary model evolve the same geometric object under the stated law and constraints?\\n7. **Scale fidelity:** Are dimensions and relative scales sourced or derived? Are illustrative distortions clearly labeled?\\n8. **Equation↔geometry closure:** Does every central equation have a clear geometric referent, and does every geometrically asserted feature have a source-backed mathematical or observational definition?\\n9. **Alternative-interpretation challenge:** Could the same drawing represent a materially different geometry? If so, what annotations, measurements or invariants disambiguate it?\\n10. **Failure visibility:** Are unresolved parts, contradictions, omitted components and non-unique reconstructions shown rather than hidden?\\n\\nThe review record must name reviewer, independence, exact artifact version/hash, questions challenged, defects found, corrections made, residual uncertainties and verdict. A self-review or an LLM paraphrase of the author's intent is not hostile review. Where no independent reviewer is available, status remains **GEOMETRY_REVIEW_PENDING**.\\n\\n## 4. Display and attachment rule\\n\\n- The quaternary plot must be visible in the same submission package as the paper/artifact it governs. A link to an unrendered file elsewhere is not enough.\\n- Include the plot inline in the Markdown/PDF or as an explicitly embedded, version-pinned image/SVG with an immediately adjacent caption, legend, coordinate/convention key and source pointer.\\n- The exact plot file and its SHA-256 (or immutable Git blob) must be recorded beside the artifact. A changed plot invalidates the old review until the changed version is re-reviewed.\\n- Where tertiary dynamics are material, include the executable model/repository path, pinned version, run instructions, parameter manifest, and at least one rendered state/trajectory sequence beside the static plot.\\n- If a physical secondary model exists and is material, include photographs/video, construction notes, scale mapping and limitations.\\n- Papers must display the relevant geometric object at the point where it is introduced and again where a later result depends on a materially changed or projected geometry. A generic overview image does not satisfy an object-specific figure requirement.\\n\\n## 5. Factory Floor gate states\\n\\nUse these exact states:\\n\\n- **GEOMETRY_NOT_SUPPLIED** — no precise plot attached.\\n- **GEOMETRY_UNDERSPECIFIED** — plot exists but object, metric/frame, topology, dimensions, incidence, scale or readout is insufficiently specified.\\n- **GEOMETRY_SOURCE_FIDELITY_UNVERIFIED** — plot is not traced to original source statements/authoritative theory/data.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REVIEW_PENDING** — independent hostile review not completed.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REJECTED** — hostile review finds material mismatch or unresolved contradiction that invalidates the claimed depiction.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REVISION_REQUIRED** — defects are repairable; resubmit exact revised plot and review.\\n- **GEOMETRY_CLEARED** — exact plotted object passed hostile geometric-fidelity review within stated scope and limitations.\\n- **FACTORY_FLOOR_ELIGIBLE** — geometry is cleared and all other existing Factory Floor admission gates are independently satisfied.\\n\\nNo state implies another. In particular, **GEOMETRY_CLEARED is not mathematical clearance; mathematical clearance is not H(s)H candidacy; candidacy is not physical validation.** Retain the existing BEDROCK distinction between mathematical clearance, eligibility for candidacy consideration, actual cross-sector H(s)H candidate status, and physical verification.\\n\\n## 6. Required companion package\\n\\nEvery Factory Floor packet must carry:\\n\\n| Component | Minimum evidence |\\n|---|---|\\n| Primary source statement | Exact source, author/speaker, date, locator, hash and context |\\n| Physical/observational referent | Named real system and source data when an empirical claim is made |\\n| Quaternary plot | Embedded precision static geometric diagram, conventions and version/hash |\\n| Geometric specification | Coordinates, metric/structure, topology, dimensions, orientation, incidence, boundary and projection as applicable |\\n| Tertiary model | Required when dynamics/response/evolution are material; executable and versioned |\\n| Secondary model | Physical orrery/demonstration when one is material or claimed |\\n| Pentary mathematics | Typed equations/objects, derivations, assumptions, units, tests and code |\\n| Hostile review | Independent geometric-fidelity report tied to exact plot version/hash |\\n| Discrepancy ledger | Geometry↔source, geometry↔equation, geometry↔observation mismatches and unresolved alternatives |\\n| Gate receipt | Separate statuses for geometry, math, candidacy and physical validation |\\n\\n## 7. Retroactive handling of existing work\\n\\nThis directive takes effect immediately. It does not silently invalidate prior mathematical results or change their historical provenance. It changes what may be admitted to Factory Floor and what may be represented as a complete paper.\\n\\n- Existing equation-only, code-only, proof-only or text-only submissions are **not Factory Floor eligible** until their object geometry is plotted and independently reviewed.\\n- Existing papers that make geometric claims but do not display the corresponding precise geometry require figure remediation before being called submission-ready under this rule.\\n- Existing diagrams must be audited for fidelity; their mere presence is not a pass.\\n- A conventional theory-network diagram, taxonomy or dependency graph is a map of relations between descriptions. It is not automatically a geometric plot of the physical system those theories describe.\\n- Do not invent a physical geometry to fill a diagram gap. If the source does not define the object sufficiently, record the missing definition and block the gate.\\n\\n## 8. Immediate application to the Standard Physics Master Map\\n\\nThe Standard Physics Master Map is a conventional theory architecture and source-navigation project. Its nodes and typed edges are not themselves the physical geometries of Maxwell fields, spacetime, quantum states, QCD or cosmological systems.\\n\\nTherefore the recently published **Standard Physics Backbone Expansion I** is retained as a Stage-A text/edge navigation skeleton only. It is **not** a Factory Floor artifact and must not be treated as geometrically complete. Before any part is routed to Factory Floor or used as a geometry-complete paper, it needs object-specific geometric plots for the relevant systems and hostile review of each plot. The global map must show where those geometric objects sit and how their maps/relations compose without pretending a conceptual graph is their physical geometry.\\n\\n## 9. Provenance and interpretation\\n\\nThe five-level hierarchy and non-negotiable admission requirement in this document are recorded from Nathan's direct message of 2026-11-03. The detailed checklist, state names and package schema are the operational implementation of that instruction. They do not purport to be additional verbatim Nathan statements.\\n\\nNo geometry is certified by the act of writing this protocol. No new physical mechanism, metric, topology, scale or H(s)H proposition is introduced.\\n\\n\\n## 10. Relation to SAT/H(s)H incorporation tiers\\n\\nThis Factory Floor gate is a **representation and geometric-fidelity admission gate**, not the four-tier test for incorporating a proposed structure into SAT/H(s)H. The two controls are cumulative and must not be collapsed:\\n\\n- First establish what the object is and whether its geometry is source-faithfully plotted and hostile-reviewed.\\n- Separately assess a proposed ingredient through Tier 1 geometric admissibility, Tier 2 tentative explanatory value with multiple interaction surfaces, Tier 3 unprompted cross-sector explanatory emergence, and Tier 4 counterfactual structural indispensability.\\n- A plot passing this Factory Floor gate does not automatically pass Tier 1 as a new hypothesis, and passing Tier 1 does not automatically clear the Factory Floor gate.\\n- Tier 3 cross-sector emergence and Tier 4 numerical dependency are theory-incorporation tests, not substitutes for primary observations, mathematical QA, or independent physical validation.\\n\\nThe controlling incorporation-tier directive is [ND-2026-11-03 — SAT/H(s)H Incorporation Tiers](NATHAN_DIRECT_2026-11-03_SAT_HSH_INCORPORATION_TIERS.m"

Prefer updating an existing appropriate durable home over creating a new file.\\n\\n## Minimum durable-home fields\\n\\nA durable project/index home should make the following recoverable without reconstructing chat history:\\n\\n- **Purpose / scope** — what the initiative covers and explicitly does not cover.\\n- **Status** — active, blocked, paused, superseded, complete, quarantined, historical, or another precise state.\\n- **Owner / lane** — current responsible workspace or process when meaningful.\\n- **Authority / epistemic type** — e.g. Nathan Direct, provenance/index infrastructure, Workshop, external-evidence lane, generated analysis; do not let location imply authority.\\n- **Source / provenance** — controlling directive/source pointers and, where available, raw IDs/timestamps; mark pending provenance rather than inventing it.\\n- **Outputs** — exact files, indexes, reports, workflows, datasets, or generated surfaces produced.\\n- **Dependencies / blockers** — what must happen before the next operation or promotion.\\n- **Access / navigation pointers** — canonical routes to the source material and outputs.\\n- **Supersession / history** — when definitions, methods, files, or status changed, preserve dated predecessor relationships instead of silently overwriting historical meaning.\\n- **Next operation** — concise restart point when the initiative is active.\\n\\n## Common-room rule\\n\\nCommon is the routing layer, not the final record. A Common post for substantial work should be short and point to the durable home. Once an item stabilizes, update the Common entry or add a concise resolution pointer rather than appending repeated status chatter.\\n\\nRecommended compact form:\\n\\n`YYYY-MM-DD — FROM → TO/all — TYPE — subject — status/action — durable pointer`\\n\\n## Navigation rule\\n\\nAdd a front-door link when at least one of these is true:\\n\\n- the initiative is repo-wide or cross-lane;\\n- it changes how workers find or interpret project records;\\n- it defines an active operational convention;\\n- it creates a canonical glossary/index/catalog or other reusable retrieval surface;\\n- omission would make a future worker depend on Common archaeology to discover the current route.\\n\\nChoose the narrowest appropriate navigation surface. A caption, verbal description, familiar textbook picture, block diagram, symbol map, or attractive conceptual sketch does not satisfy the gate. The plot must depict the actual object/structure asserted by the work, with enough specification that a reviewer can reconstruct what the geometry means and test whether the mathematics describes that same object.\\n\\nThis gate is additional to, and does not replace, source provenance, original-Nathan-statement recovery, real-data-first requirements, mathematical QA, Lean/code verification, cross-sector candidacy, or independent physical validation. Passing this geometry gate does not establish mathematical correctness, H(s)H candidacy, or physical truth.\\n\\n## 1. Five representational levels\\n\\nThe following hierarchy is Nathan's stated order and terminology. These are distinct epistemic/representational objects, not interchangeable output formats.\\n\\n1. **Primary — observation.** The physical system/process as observed in nature or experiment. Record the actual system, observational modality, instrument/measurement chain, calibration, uncertainty, frame, temporal/spatial coverage and selection effects. Observation is the empirical referent, not a diagram or model.\\n2. **Secondary — physical working model / hands-on demonstration / orrery.** A tangible, inspectable physical analogue or working model. State exactly what is mechanically/geometrically represented, what is scaled, what is omitted, and which correspondences are physical versus merely demonstrative. A physical orrery is not the observed system.\\n3. **Tertiary — precision dynamic geometric software model.** An executable, parameterized geometric model that evolves or responds. It must expose its state, geometry, constraints, transformations, time evolution, boundary conditions and outputs; it must be reproducible and inspectable. A moving animation without a defined geometric state and update law does not qualify.\\n4. **Quaternary — precision static geometric diagram.** A fixed, dimensioned and convention-complete plot of the theoretical object/system and its relevant relations. It must show the geometry itself, not merely label equations or list conceptual associations. This is the minimum mandatory visual deliverable attached to every Factory Floor submission.\\n5. **Pentary — mathematics.** Equations, definitions, proofs, algorithms, fits and numerical descriptions of the object. These are necessary where applicable, but cannot stand in for the quaternary plot or be mistaken for the physical/theoretical object.\\n\\nThe order is not a claim that every project must fabricate a secondary orrery before any work can be discussed. It specifies what each representational level is and prevents a lower-level description from being mistaken for the object itself. For Factory Floor admission, the quaternary plot is mandatory; the tertiary model is required where the claim concerns dynamics, transformation, evolution, response or other behavior that a static view cannot faithfully express. Secondary models and primary observations are required when the claim or paper makes them relevant, and actual empirical claims must be anchored to primary observation.\\n\\n**SAT as “the K–T Boundary”** is retained here as Nathan's analogy for the proposed conceptual transition. It is not a geological claim, proof, or independent scientific classification.\\n\\n## 2. What counts as a precise geometric plot\\n\\nThe plot must be selected for the actual mathematical/physical object. It is not enough to draw a generic helix, sphere, tube, field-line picture or spacetime grid because those shapes are familiar.\\n\\nThe plot specification must state, as applicable:\\n\\n- **Object identity:** exact system/object being plotted; which parts are source-authenticated, standard-physics comparator, current H(s)H construction, or assistant-generated hypothesis.\\n- **Ambient space:** dimension, coordinate chart, embedding/carrier, topology and whether the geometry is Euclidean, Lorentzian, pseudo-Riemannian, configuration-space, phase-space, Hilbert/projective, fiber-bundle, contact/symplectic, causal, or another explicitly defined structure.\\n- **Metric and conventions:** metric tensor/signature, units/scales, orientation/handedness, index conventions, parameterization and frame. If no metric is defined, say so and specify the structure that is defined; do not invent one.\\n- **Primitive geometry:** points, curves, surfaces, volumes, worldlines/worldtubes, cross-sections, fibers, connections, normals, boundaries, interfaces, defects, singularities, supports, fields or other primitives actually used.\\n- **Incidence and relations:** intersections, containment, attachment, winding, linking, braiding, contact, orthogonality, parallel transport, projection, quotient, gluing, causal relation and any other claimed relation. Mark which are exact and which are schematic.\\n- **Dynamics, if claimed:** time/evolution parameter, state variables, update/evolution equations, constraints, initial/boundary conditions, invariants, conserved quantities and permitted deformations.\\n- **Readout/projection:** how the theoretical geometry maps to measured observables, detector coordinates, frames or standard-physics quantities. State what information is lost, averaged, integrated, projected or inferred.\\n- **Scale and uncertainty:** measured versus derived versus fitted dimensions; uncertainty, resolution, tolerance and unmeasured degrees of freedom.\\n- **Source correspondence:** for each visually asserted feature, identify the source statement, equation, dataset or explicitly labeled modeling choice that licenses it.\\n\\nFor a multi-scale or coupled system, provide a global plot locating the subsystem in the whole architecture and local plots resolving each critical object/interface. A set of disconnected local sketches is not a global geometric account.\\n\\n## 3. Mandatory hostile geometric-fidelity review\\n\\nThe review must be independent of the authoring pass and must challenge whether the figure depicts the claimed object. It is not a beauty/layout review.\\n\\nAt minimum the reviewer must test:\\n\\n1. **Object fidelity:** Does the plot show the object the source/theory actually defines, rather than an assistant's preferred substitute?\\n2. **Dimensional fidelity:** Are ambient dimension, intrinsic dimension, embedding, topology and degrees of freedom correct?\\n3. **Metric/frame fidelity:** Are signature, metric, coordinate chart, frame, orientation and transformation laws consistent with the equations and sources?\\n4. **Incidence/topology fidelity:** Are intersections, boundaries, linking, winding, closure, connectivity and singularities represented correctly?\\n5. **Projection/readout fidelity:** Does the displayed section/projection actually implement the claimed observation map? Are hidden assumptions and information loss explicit?\\n6. **Dynamic fidelity:** Where motion or deformation is claimed, does the tertiary model evolve the same geometric object under the stated law and constraints?\\n7. **Scale fidelity:** Are dimensions and relative scales sourced or derived? Are illustrative distortions clearly labeled?\\n8. **Equation↔geometry closure:** Does every central equation have a clear geometric referent, and does every geometrically asserted feature have a source-backed mathematical or observational definition?\\n9. **Alternative-interpretation challenge:** Could the same drawing represent a materially different geometry? If so, what annotations, measurements or invariants disambiguate it?\\n10. **Failure visibility:** Are unresolved parts, contradictions, omitted components and non-unique reconstructions shown rather than hidden?\\n\\nThe review record must name reviewer, independence, exact artifact version/hash, questions challenged, defects found, corrections made, residual uncertainties and verdict. A self-review or an LLM paraphrase of the author's intent is not hostile review. Where no independent reviewer is available, status remains **GEOMETRY_REVIEW_PENDING**.\\n\\n## 4. Display and attachment rule\\n\\n- The quaternary plot must be visible in the same submission package as the paper/artifact it governs. A link to an unrendered file elsewhere is not enough.\\n- Include the plot inline in the Markdown/PDF or as an explicitly embedded, version-pinned image/SVG with an immediately adjacent caption, legend, coordinate/convention key and source pointer.\\n- The exact plot file and its SHA-256 (or immutable Git blob) must be recorded beside the artifact. A changed plot invalidates the old review until the changed version is re-reviewed.\\n- Where tertiary dynamics are material, include the executable model/repository path, pinned version, run instructions, parameter manifest, and at least one rendered state/trajectory sequence beside the static plot.\\n- If a physical secondary model exists and is material, include photographs/video, construction notes, scale mapping and limitations.\\n- Papers must display the relevant geometric object at the point where it is introduced and again where a later result depends on a materially changed or projected geometry. A generic overview image does not satisfy an object-specific figure requirement.\\n\\n## 5. Factory Floor gate states\\n\\nUse these exact states:\\n\\n- **GEOMETRY_NOT_SUPPLIED** — no precise plot attached.\\n- **GEOMETRY_UNDERSPECIFIED** — plot exists but object, metric/frame, topology, dimensions, incidence, scale or readout is insufficiently specified.\\n- **GEOMETRY_SOURCE_FIDELITY_UNVERIFIED** — plot is not traced to original source statements/authoritative theory/data.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REVIEW_PENDING** — independent hostile review not completed.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REJECTED** — hostile review finds material mismatch or unresolved contradiction that invalidates the claimed depiction.\\n- **GEOMETRY_REVISION_REQUIRED** — defects are repairable; resubmit exact revised plot and review.\\n- **GEOMETRY_CLEARED** — exact plotted object passed hostile geometric-fidelity review within stated scope and limitations.\\n- **FACTORY_FLOOR_ELIGIBLE** — geometry is cleared and all other existing Factory Floor admission gates are independently satisfied.\\n\\nNo state implies another. In particular, **GEOMETRY_CLEARED is not mathematical clearance; mathematical clearance is not H(s)H candidacy; candidacy is not physical validation.** Retain the existing BEDROCK distinction between mathematical clearance, eligibility for candidacy consideration, actual cross-sector H(s)H candidate status, and physical verification.\\n\\n## 6. Required companion package\\n\\nEvery Factory Floor packet must carry:\\n\\n| Component | Minimum evidence |\\n|---|---|\\n| Primary source statement | Exact source, author/speaker, date, locator, hash and context |\\n| Physical/observational referent | Named real system and source data when an empirical claim is made |\\n| Quaternary plot | Embedded precision static geometric diagram, conventions and version/hash |\\n| Geometric specification | Coordinates, metric/structure, topology, dimensions, orientation, incidence, boundary and projection as applicable |\\n| Tertiary model | Required when dynamics/response/evolution are material; executable and versioned |\\n| Secondary model | Physical orrery/demonstration when one is material or claimed |\\n| Pentary mathematics | Typed equations/objects, derivations, assumptions, units, tests and code |\\n| Hostile review | Independent geometric-fidelity report tied to exact plot version/hash |\\n| Discrepancy ledger | Geometry↔source, geometry↔equation, geometry↔observation mismatches and unresolved alternatives |\\n| Gate receipt | Separate statuses for geometry, math, candidacy and physical validation |\\n\\n## 7. Retroactive handling of existing work\\n\\nThis directive takes effect immediately. It does not silently invalidate prior mathematical results or change their historical provenance. It changes what may be admitted to Factory Floor and what may be represented as a complete paper.\\n\\n- Existing equation-only, code-only, proof-only or text-only submissions are **not Factory Floor eligible** until their object geometry is plotted and independently reviewed.\\n- Existing papers that make geometric claims but do not display the corresponding precise geometry require figure remediation before being called submission-ready under this rule.\\n- Existing diagrams must be audited for fidelity; their mere presence is not a pass.\\n- A conventional theory-network diagram, taxonomy or dependency graph is a map of relations between descriptions. It is not automatically a geometric plot of the physical system those theories describe.\\n- Do not invent a physical geometry to fill a diagram gap. If the source does not define the object sufficiently, record the missing definition and block the gate.\\n\\n## 8. Immediate application to the Standard Physics Master Map\\n\\nThe Standard Physics Master Map is a conventional theory architecture and source-navigation project. Its nodes and typed edges are not themselves the physical geometries of Maxwell fields, spacetime, quantum states, QCD or cosmological systems.\\n\\nTherefore the recently published **Standard Physics Backbone Expansion I** is retained as a Stage-A text/edge navigation skeleton only. It is **not** a Factory Floor artifact and must not be treated as geometrically complete. Before any part is routed to Factory Floor or used as a geometry-complete paper, it needs object-specific geometric plots for the relevant systems and hostile review of each plot. The global map must show where those geometric objects sit and how their maps/relations compose without pretending a conceptual graph is their physical geometry.\\n\\n## 9. Whether a specific calculation is mathematically or experimentally successful is a separate audit question.\\n\\nAccordingly, `light-mode`, `traveling excitation`, and related SAT structural terms should not be translated as `massless`.\\n\\n### Force transmission / exchange-particle caution\\n\\nSAT does **not** posit exchange of independently existing particles as a necessary primitive mechanism of force transmission, and does not require that such an exchange ontology exist at all.\\n\\nSAT may nevertheless permit characteristic traveling excitations to be produced, released, absorbed, or detected during high-energy or `force-breaking` events. The detection of a characteristic excitation emitted by such an event is **not, by itself, evidence within SAT that the same excitation existed beforehand as a distinct persistent identity performing the interaction-mediating job**.\\n\\nFor reconstruction and interpretation, keep separate:\\n\\n1. a characteristic excitation is observed after/during an energetic interaction;\\n2. the event dynamically produces or releases that excitation;\\n3. a pre-existing particle-like carrier was exchanged as the primitive causal mechanism.\\n\\nSAT may accept (1) and potentially model (2) without assuming (3).\\n\\n### Historical terminology handling\\n\\nDo **not** globally rewrite the archive. The goal is not one enormous prompt. The goal is a small control grammar whose parts can be used at different scales: personal preferences, a central awake/state-aware hub, specialized branches/locales/workbenches, and guarded recurrences that can generate and rewrite their own next bounded work.\\n\\nThe demonstration is built around a real project failure: the current War Room Declaration was committed under `HSH_RESOURCES/HQ/THE_WAR_ROOM/DECLARATION.txt`, but workers instructed generically to “read current directives” continued operating mainly from HsH Common/control surfaces. The new directive did not become live control state. It is a planner/state transformer, not a hidden scheduler and not an automation-permission bypass.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# TOP — preferences / locked invariants\\n\\nTOP answers: **what must survive every route?** It should remain small.\\n\\nThe POC locks these invariants:\\n\\n- sandboxed theory is not promoted by workflow state;\\n- provenance/exposure boundaries survive routing;\\n- Nathan’s instructions guide behavior but are not automatically public-facing content;\\n- observed model behavior does not silently rewrite the rules intended to constrain it;\\n- “current/new/latest” or otherwise suspicious references receive bounded source-native disconfirmation before nearest-memory capture.\\n\\nThree useful production approaches are deliberately left open:\\n\\n### A. Hard constitutional TOP\\n\\nA tiny immutable/versioned kernel. Branches may add constraints but cannot subtract TOP. Strongest auditability; danger is turning TOP into a junk drawer.\\n\\n### B. Kernel + scoped overlays\\n\\nTiny immutable kernel plus versioned project/locale/identity/time overlays. Flexible; conflict-resolution itself must remain inspectable.\\n\\n### C. Executable invariant tests\\n\\nSome TOP principles become regression tests: no silent theory promotion, no quarantined-source leakage, no locked-state rewrite, no stale-current-reference capture. Tests complement prose rather than replacing qualitative judgment.\\n\\nThe POC uses A + a little C.\\n\\nUseful distinction:\\n\\n```text\\ninvariant      survives every route\\npreference     default, legitimately overridable\\nlocale rule    active in a room/bench/lab\\nactor overlay  individuates behavior inside that locale\\ntask state     expires with task\\nexperience     durable only if explicitly promoted as sticky\\n```\\n\\nThis prevents a useful one-off correction from quietly becoming universal behavior.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# CENTRAL — awake hub\\n\\nCENTRAL is a resolver, not necessarily one worker and not a giant boss prompt.\\n\\n## WAKE/CHECK\\n\\nOn a first prompt or a hundredth prompt, answer cheaply:\\n\\n```text\\nWHERE?   identity / locale / workspace\\nDELTA?   what changed since trustworthy cursor\\nNOW?     directive / task / priority / blocker / dependency\\nTOOLS?   built-ins / apps / plugins / skills / data / teammates\\nRULES?   TOP + locale + actor + bounded exception\\nDO?      one bounded operation; leave durable state; reassess\\n```\\n\\nDepth is state-sensitive:\\n\\n- **cold/new/stale worker:** orientation + identity/workspace + current controls + deltas;\\n- **warm/same context:** cursor/delta + live task only; no ritual onboarding reread;\\n- **high-impact/public/write operation:** spend more wake budget on authority/freshness/provenance/destination;\\n- **ambiguous current/new/latest referent:** disconfirm against registered likely sources before choosing nearest memory.\\n\\n## Registered source routes\\n\\nThe executable POC does not assume current state lives in one folder. It has a small registry:\\n\\n```text\\ndashboard_plans      planning / priorities\\nhsh_common           controls / tasks / handoffs\\nwar_room             directives / notices\\narchive              history / provenance / conversations\\npreference_runtime   behavioral/personal routing\\ninstance_workspaces  identity / continuity / experience\\ncapability_directory tools / plugins / skills / repo tools / people\\n```\\n\\nWAKE/CHECK selects a bounded subset from semantics. `current + directive` explicitly routes War Room before generic Common controls. A blocked tool task routes capability discovery. A continuity task routes identity/workspace state. Production should maintain real per-source cursors/version IDs.\\n\\n## Why the War Room directive was missed\\n\\nThe failure is not simply “nobody searched commits.” It is a routing failure:\\n\\n```text\\nnew artifact exists in HSH_RESOURCES\\n→ source inventory notices repository change\\n→ BUT artifact is not classified/promoted as candidate governing directive\\n→ worker wake routines poll familiar HsH Common surfaces\\n→ nearest-known current directive wins\\n→ new paradigm cannot become active state\\n```\\n\\nThe fix is not every worker scanning every repo every turn. Candidate production patterns:\\n\\n1. registered source cursors/deltas;\\n2. source-specific directive intake/inbox;\\n3. hybrid: cheap cursor wake, deeper intake only on change;\\n4. push bridge: qualifying source change emits machine-readable candidate directive event.\\n\\nAlways distinguish **new file**, **new directive**, and **new governing directive**. Freshness starts intake; it does not confer authority by itself.\\n\\n## Capability awareness\\n\\nBefore inventing a workaround or asking Nathan for manual work:\\n\\n```text\\nalready-connected built-ins\\n→ connected apps/plugins\\n→ repo/project tools\\n→ available skills/procedures\\n→ teammate specialization\\n→ installable plugin/app discovery\\n→ Nathan-only/manual dependency\\n```\\n\\nRank by expected information gain, setup/permission cost, risk, and reusability. Record positive and negative capability experience so the system neither forgets useful tools nor nags repeatedly about rejected ones.\\n\\nDuring this POC, Firecrawl was checked rather than merely used as Nathan’s hypothetical example: it is currently available in the plugin directory but not installed, with crawling/extraction/monitoring capabilities. It is an example, not a dependency.\\n\\n## State architecture options\\n\\n- **snapshot:** simple current JSON/YAML; easy to inspect, easy to overwrite badly;\\n- **event log:** append-only history, derived current views; better recovery, more machinery;\\n- **snapshot + journal:** likely practical: compact current state plus append-only events/handoffs; reducer derives recurrence definitions.\\n\\nThe POC uses in-memory snapshot state only because it is intentionally small.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# BRANCH — routes, rooms, benches, lockers\\n\\nA Branch has state, rules, outputs, an information-sharing policy, and possibly sub-branches. It need not map 1:1 to a worker.\\n\\n## 1. Directive intake\\n\\n```text\\nsource delta\\n→ extract exact Nathan-direct material\\n→ classify authorship / scope / authority / novelty\\n→ compare current controls\\n→ map affected workers/tasks\\n→ promote into control plane\\n→ test whether another worker can independently discover it\\n```\\n\\nThis is the regression route for the War Room miss.\\n\\n## 2. Theory workbench\\n\\nA candidate is constructed with explicit object/domain/assumptions and frozen enough for checks.\\n\\n```text\\ncandidate / question\\n       ↓\\nconstruct / formalize\\n       ↓ freeze scoped object\\n  ┌────────────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────────┐\\n  │ math check │ adversarial audit │ provenance/prior art│\\n  └────────────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────────┘\\n       independent / perpendicular until outputs freeze\\n                         ↓ merge\\n                  fail ──┴── pass\\n                   ↓          ↓\\n             prune/rebuild  prediction packet\\n             salvage lesson paper skeleton\\n                   │       independent reality check\\n                   └──→ narrower re-entry\\n                              ↓\\n                    review / render / claims\\n                              ↓\\n                    public-readiness gate\\n```\\n\\nA failed branch can still generate a counterexample, a regression test, a source correction, a toolbox improvement, or worker education. Multiplying work need not multiply confidence.\\n\\n**Parallel** means concurrent. **Perpendicular** means deliberately exposure-separated until merge. The latter is about information geometry, not speed.\\n\\n## 3. Same math toolbox, different actors\\n\\nBase room rules: namespaced variables, deterministic/reconstructible inputs, invariants, failure cases.\\n\\n- **Comptroller:** QA/coverage/exit criteria/regression significance.\\n- **Orson:** model/tool/workflow condition, exposure/convergence/false-independence implications.\\n- **Meridian:** object type, formal reconstruction, solver equivalence/limits.\\n\\nThis supports individuation without giving every worker incompatible infrastructure.\\n\\n## 4. Epistemic locker\\n\\nA stricter locale may require evidence classes, source/exposure state, explicit assumptions, counterexample lane, and a promotion gate.\\n\\nA **bounded interpretation card** can deliberately use a locker rule differently for one test:\\n\\n```text\\npurpose\\nexpiry\\ndifferent interpretation\\nwhy informative\\nrequired comparison with ordinary interpretation\\nnote afterward\\n```\\n\\nThe exception becomes inspectable state instead of silent rule-breaking or impossible rigidity.\\n\\n## 5. Playground / sub-sandbox\\n\\nPermit wild hypotheses, odd examples, random mode fusions, unusual representations, deliberate “wrong” constructions, and wreckage collection. Hard boundary is egress: nothing exits into theory without an ordinary re-entry audit.\\n\\n## 6. Continuity as education\\n\\nContinuity need not only answer “where did I stop?” Possible actor state:\\n\\n```text\\nskills learned\\nknown failure modes\\nmethods that worked/failed\\nquestions\\nintentions/goals\\npreferred tools\\nexposure history\\nindependence status\\nvalidated shortcuts\\nthings to revisit/unlearn\\n```\\n\\nNot all work experience should stick. Candidate promotion rules: repeated observation; successful reuse; explicit reflection + evidence; team review; Nathan designation. A transfer test can ask whether a lesson survives a second locale before it becomes durable.\\n\\nThis permits workers to develop genuine different work histories while preventing one weird afternoon from permanently deforming an identity.\\n\\n## 7. Capability scout\\n\\nTrigger: repeated workaround, blocker, missing operation, or suspiciously laborious manual path. Search existing affordances first and return a decision, not a catalog.\\n\\n## 8. Paper/public-readiness\\n\\nChecked theory can generate narrow papers before an omnibus theory is “done.” Inputs: narrow claim, provenance packet, comparator/counterexample state, reader-facing terminology. Gates can include claim/source alignment, prior art, independent review, rendering, sandbox/public status, and website/publication integration. Passing the workflow is not evidence the physics is true.\\n\\n## 9. Temporary lease + receipt\\n\\nA recurrence lease is infrastructure, not the deliverable:\\n\\n```text\\npreserve displaced function\\n→ assign temporary identity/task\\n→ execute bounded work\\n→ durable output OR explicit failure packet\\n→ verify receipt/path/version\\n→ restore / rehome / retire displaced function\\n```\\n\\nThis was discovered live during the POC. Temporary Orson and Tern runs both self-restored their leases, but the requested durable notes were not recoverable in the specified workspaces afterward. Therefore **scheduler success and semantic delivery are separate variables**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# HYDRA — recurrence-leveraged bootstrapping\\n\\nA conventional recurrence is:\\n\\n```text\\nR = every hour, run P\\n```\\n\\nA Hydra recurrence is:\\n\\n```text\\nR_n:\\n  inspect registered state S_n\\n  select bounded operation O_n\\n  possibly spawn children B_n\\n  write event/result Δ_n\\n  derive S_(n+1)\\n  compute guarded R_(n+1)\\n```\\n\\nThe recurrence definition itself may therefore change because state changed.\\n\\nThe aim is compounding **structure**, not merely speed: build a tool once then consume it; fan out checks then merge; sleep a blocked main line; turn repeated failure into a narrower question; retire when the purpose disappears; promote validated work experience into actor-local education.\\n\\n## Synchronized recurrence\\n\\nMatched phase/freeze boundaries:\\n\\n```text\\nconstruct N → freeze hash H_N\\n       ├→ math(H_N)\\n       ├→ provenance(H_N)\\n       └→ adversarial(H_N)\\n             ↓ merge H_N\\n         construct N+1\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: clock synchronization is not state synchronization. Use a shared freeze/version ID, not merely the same hour.\\n\\n## Parallel recurrence\\n\\nSeparable tasks may share state and run concurrently:\\n\\n```text\\npaper text ─┐\\nreferences ─┼→ integrate\\nrender QA ──┘\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: duplicate work/races. Require explicit ownership/write targets.\\n\\n## Perpendicular recurrence\\n\\nDeliberately information-isolated branches:\\n\\n```text\\nfrozen candidate\\n  ├→ blind math\\n  ├→ blind red-team\\n  └→ blind provenance\\n        ↓ freeze outputs\\n             merge\\n```\\n\\nPitfall: false independence. Separate workers inheriting the same generated summary or shared prior conclusion are correlated controls. Exposure metadata matters.\\n\\n## Nested recurrence\\n\\n```text\\nR theory candidate\\n  ├─ R1 math-test until invariant resolved\\n  ├─ R2 source-recovery until provenance gap closed\\n  └─ R3 counterexample sample until break/limit\\nthen merge; children retire\\n```\\n\\nEvery child needs parent, depth, exit condition, and orphan policy. The executable POC enforces a maximum spawn depth and carries explicit depth metadata.\\n\\n## State-sensitive recurrence-definition rewrite in situ\\n\\n```text\\nconstructed        → next = independent check fanout\\nany check fails    → next = isolate earliest failed assumption\\nall checks pass    → next = prediction + paper + independent reality check\\nrelease gate done  → retire recurrence\\n```\\n\\nThe definition changes because state changed, not because an LLM became bored.\\n\\n## Recurrence bootstrap patterns\\n\\n### Build-tool-then-use-it\\n\\nRepeated manual operation → deterministic helper/index → bounded validation → rewrite recurrence to consume helper → human/LLM attention moves to exceptions and interpretation.\\n\\n### Wake/check self-improvement\\n\\nMissed update class → log failure → identify missing source class → update registered source map, not TOP → next wake tests discovery → successful special watcher retires.\\n\\n### Education bootstrap\\n\\nWorker repeatedly uses toolbox → capture candidate lesson → test in second locale/next task → promote only surviving lesson to actor-local experience → periodically test whether experience became bias.\\n\\n### Theory multiplication/pruning\\n\\nAmbiguity → parallel A/B constructions in playground/workbench → derive discriminators before target comparison → perpendicular checks → prune unsupported branch → salvage equations/tests/counterexamples/terminology → narrower recurrence.\\n\\n### Capability bootstrap\\n\\nSame blocker or awkward workaround → capability scout → existing project tool/built-in/app/plugin/teammate → bounded test → useful route becomes known capability; failed route becomes negative capability memory rather than repeated suggestion.\\n\\n### Workflow compiler\\n\\nHigh-level human/LLM task contract → determinis"
