Enforcement belongs server/index side.\\n\\n## Query language — current\\n\\nUnqualified terms search record body text.\\n\\nCurrent fields:\\n- `body:` — explicit body phrase/term.\\n- `math:` — conservative notation-normalized mathematical substring search.\\n- `name:` — basename; supports shell-style `*`, `?`, character classes.\\n- `path:` — source path; same glob support.\\n- `ext:` — extension, without leading dot.\\n- `type:` / `kind:` — indexed record kind.\\n- `has:` — mechanically established properties such as conversation-source, pdf-source, text-source, message-id, conversation-id, viewer.\\n- `author:` / `speaker:`\\n- `role:`\\n- `title:`\\n- `conversation:` / `cid:`\\n- `date:` including `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD`\\n- `status:` — lexical status-signal retrieval only.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n```text\\nname:*2026.txt\\nname:*26.txt OR name:26*.txt\\n(path:*SAT_CONVOS_20* AND ext:txt) AND body:\\\"star shaped\\\"\\nauthor:Nathan AND (holonomy NEAR/12 glitch)\\nmath:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"\\n```\\n\\n## Mathematical retrieval roadmap\\n\\n### M0 — notation normalization — IMPLEMENTED\\n\\nNormalize common presentation differences while preserving raw source:\\n- selected Unicode/LaTeX/plain symbol aliases;\\n- multiplication/division glyphs;\\n- Unicode minus / approximation;\\n- whitespace;\\n- simple LaTeX fractions.\\n\\nA notation match is **not algebraic equivalence**. Current negative acceptance control requires `math:\\\"4*pi*B=3\\\"` not to match `B=3/(4*pi)` merely because a human can rearrange it.\\n\\n### M1 — expression extraction\\n\\nIdentify probable equation spans from LaTeX delimiters, display blocks, inline formulas, Unicode/plain equations and code-like math. Store:\\n- exact raw expression;\\n- source locator;\\n- surrounding context;\\n- notation-normalized form;\\n- parse status;\\n- parser/version.\\n\\nNever discard `UNPARSED` expressions.\\n\\n### M2 — structural parsing\\n\\nParse supported expressions into a symbolic AST. Add:\\n- `contains:` structural/subexpression search;\\n- symbol/function/operator facets;\\n- equation-shape fingerprints;\\n- alpha-renaming option only when explicitly requested.\\n\\n### M3 — algebraic relation\\n\\nAdd conservative CAS-backed relationship testing:\\n- `EXACT`\\n- `NORMALIZED-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `ALGEBRAICALLY-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `CONTAINS-SUBEXPRESSION`\\n- `NUMERICALLY-CONSISTENT`\\n- `POSSIBLE-RELATION`\\n- `UNPARSED`\\n\\nTarget query: `equiv:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"`.\\n\\nCAS transformations must be recorded and bounded. Do not silently equate expressions under unstated domain assumptions.\\n\\n### M4 — equation genealogy / derivation archaeology\\n\\nTarget `derive:` searches documented archive relationships rather than inventing a derivation. Desired chain:\\n`first known occurrence → reformulation → substitution → numerical evaluation → cross-sector reuse → correction/reversal → latest known occurrence`.\\n\\nChronology alone never establishes supersession. What exact source object matched?\\n2. What corpus/profile allowed it?\\n3. What exact query clause matched?\\n4. Where in the record did it match?\\n5. A parser should accept a held-out battery of equations\\nand output:\\n1. the normalized form;\\n2. characteristic scales implied by the original coefficients;\\n3. dimensionless groups;\\n4. operator-order and algebraic structure;\\n5. a residual class.\\nThe allowed transformation grammar should be frozen before scoring the holdout set.\\nThree outcomes are then distinguishable:\\n1. No compression. Residual classes proliferate or require discretionary retuning.\\n2. Representational compression. A small fixed grammar and a small stable residual vocabulary organize many\\nsectors.\\n3. Stronger structure. Residual relations inferred from one family correctly organize quantitative relations in\\nindependent holdout families without additional fitting.\\nOnly the third outcome would motivate claims beyond methodology.\\n8. Conclusion\\nThe map w = ct is elementary. Used once, it is mostly a familiar change of units. Used as a frozen cross-sector audit,\\nit poses a disciplined question:\\nWhat disappears, what survives, and do the survivors recur in a small number of forms?\\nThe demonstrations below show both positive and negative behavior. That is the intended result. The method is\\nnot designed to make every equation fit; it is designed to turn the pattern of fit and non-fit into structured data.\\n6\\n\\n\\n## Page 7\\n\\nDRAFT\\nA. I have confirmed that the PDF, TeX source, and extracted text belong to the same document.\n\n**The paper is _Metric Symmetry to Reveal the Grain_, by Nathan McKnight and Janus C. Sol, dated September 9, 2026.** It is marked DRAFT.\n\n| Archive artifact | Path | SHA / identifier |\n|---|---|---|\n| PDF | `DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.pdf` | SHA-256 `14ecb786…08b06` |\n| TeX source | `DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.tex` | Git blob `52c7183e…dcb1` |\n| Extracted text | `_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.txt` | Git blob `e7e16f5a…cb79` |\n\nThe extraction record says it was produced from the PDF on September 10, using PyMuPDF, with all 10 pages extracted and no OCR required. I’m reading the full text against the TeX source now, including the appendices and bibliography. \n\n## What the paper is doing\n\nThe central proposal is a **cross-sector normalization audit**. It takes a single fixed coordinate transformation,\n\n\\[\nw=ct,\n\\]\n\napplies it wherever time occurs in a physical equation, and then records what remains after permitted invertible transformations.\n\nIts governing principle is:\n\n> Normalize without loss; record the residue. Deviation is data.\n\nThe paper is not trying to make all physical laws collapse into one equation. It is trying to establish a common representational framework in which similarities and differences among physical laws become easier to identify.\n\n### The structure of the argument\n\n| Section | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| 1. Question | Establishes the problem and distinguishes the proposed method from ordinary dimensional analysis. |\n| 2. Protocol | Defines the base transformation, admissible secondary transformations and residual. |\n| 3. Calibration | Tests the transformation against wave propagation, Maxwell theory, quantum mechanics, diffusion, nonlinear oscillation and central forces. |\n| 4. Controls | Shows where normalization should not eliminate structural differences. |\n| 5. Measurement | Identifies recurring dimensional conversions and proposes a residual taxonomy. |\n| 6. Prior art | Places the method alongside dimensional analysis, natural units, similarity theory and Lie-symmetry methods. |\n| 7. Next step | Proposes a computational, preregistered test using equations withheld from the initial classification. |\n| Appendix | Supplies a broad cross-sector equation battery and an interpretive classification ledger. |\n\n### The most interesting results\n\n**1. The method distinguishes coefficient normalization from structural equivalence.**\n\nFor a wave equation,\n\n\\[\n\\partial_t^2\\psi=u^2\\nabla^2\\psi,\n\\]\n\nthe transformation produces\n\n\\[\n\\partial_w^2\\psi=\n\\left(\\frac{u}{c}\\right)^2\\nabla^2\\psi.\n\\]\n\nWhen \\(u=c\\), the coefficients balance, but the Lorentzian sign structure remains. The transformation does not erase the distinction between the temporal and spatial parts of the operator.\n\n**2. Physical constants frequently reappear as characteristic lengths.**\n\nSome examples:\n\n| Original quantity | Normalized representation |\n|---|---|\n| Frequency \\(\\omega\\) | \\(\\omega/c\\) |\n| Diffusion coefficient \\(D\\) | \\(D/c\\) |\n| Quantum mass scale \\(\\hbar/m\\) | Compton length \\(\\hbar/(mc)\\) |\n| Gravitational coupling \\(GM\\) | Gravitational length \\(GM/c^2\\) |\n\nThis is one of the paper's central observations: normalization does not necessarily remove a parameter. It can reveal its geometric dimensional role.\n\n**3. The residuals are the actual object of study.**\n\nThe paper identifies recurring categories:\n\n- Derivative order\n- Characteristic lengths and inverse lengths\n- Dimensionless couplings\n- Nonlinearity\n- Dissipation\n- Dispersion\n- Discrete spacing\n- Source and boundary structure\n- Metric signature\n- Topology\n- Absence of a temporal variable\n\nThe distinction between a normalized coefficient and a surviving structural feature is important throughout.\n\n**4. It deliberately includes failures.**\n\nThe static equations are particularly useful controls. Laplace's equation, the ideal gas law, the first law of thermodynamics and static Hooke's law do not change under the base transformation.\n\nThe paper treats this as a successful negative result, not a defect. The normalization must not manufacture temporal structure where none appears in the original equation.\n\n---\n\n## My technical reading\n\nI think the strongest idea here is not the substitution \\(w=ct\\). That is standard. It is the attempt to build a **fixed transformation grammar and a systematic residual inventory** across otherwise unrelated mathematical descriptions.\n\nThere are several important points to develop.\n\n### 1. The residual needs a more rigorous mathematical definition\n\nThe paper defines\n\n\\[\nR(E\\mid T)=\n\\text{information in }E\n\\text{ that remains after canonicalization under }T.\n\\]\n\nThat is a useful conceptual definition, but it is not yet an operational mathematical object.\n\nA more rigorous formulation would define:\n\n- The space of admissible equations.\n- The transformation class acting on that space.\n- The equivalence relation induced by the transformations.\n- The invariants preserved by that action.\n- A representation of each equation's residual structure.\n\nThis could turn the residual taxonomy into a mathematically testable classification rather than an interpretive ledger.\n\n### 2. The transformation grammar needs to be frozen more precisely\n\nThe paper permits secondary transformations if they are invertible, recorded, and universal or algebraically determined by parameters already present.\n\nThat is sensible, but the boundary between an admissible universal transformation and a discretionary equation-specific transformation needs to be made explicit.\n\nOtherwise, the method risks quietly becoming ordinary nondimensionalization with a common first step.\n\n### 3. The proposed equivalence classes deserve deeper investigation\n\nThe Newtonian gravitational and Coulomb examples are especially interesting. After extracting their respective characteristic lengths, both can be represented by the same dimensionless inverse-square central-force form.\n\nThat is a genuine representational correspondence, but not physical identity.\n\nI would extend this comparison to other force laws and geometric structures, examining which aspects survive normalization and which do not. The important question is whether the resulting equivalence classes form a coherent mathematical structure.\n\n### 4. The computational proposal is the natural next stage\n\nThe paper's proposed parser should eventually produce a structured record for every equation:\n\n1. Original equation and source.\n2. Normalized equation.\n3. Applied transformations.\n4. Extracted characteristic scales.\n5. Dimensionless parameters.\n6. Operator and algebraic structure.\n7. Residual classification.\n8. Transformation provenance.\n\nThen a held-out equation battery can test whether the classification actually generalizes.\n\nThat would give the paper a much stronger empirical and mathematical foundation.\n\n---\n\n## A few source and fidelity observations\n\n- The PDF and extracted text identify the document as **_Metric Symmetry to Reveal the Grain_**.\n- The TeX source has an older PDF metadata title, *Deviation Is Data: A Cross-Sector Normalization Audit of Physical Laws*. That appears to be a leftover from an earlier title.\n- The extracted text contains the complete 10-page paper, including the equation battery and references. It was extracted without OCR.\n- The paper uses \\(w=ct\\). It does **not** contain `cw=t`, `c=wt`, or a definition of Forest Normalization.\n- The word *grain* appears in the title, but the paper does not establish a separate mathematical object called a grain.\n\nThe source files are here:\n\n- [PDF: DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.pdf](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.pdf)\n- [TeX: DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.tex](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.tex)\n- [Extracted text](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.txt)\n\n**My overall assessment:** this is a methodological paper with a promising central idea, a useful collection of demonstrations, and a sensible falsification strategy. It takes a single fixed coordinate transformation,\n\n\\[\nw=ct,\n\\]\n\napplies it wherever time occurs in a physical equation, and then records what remains after permitted invertible transformations.\n\nIts governing principle is\\:\n\n> Normalize without loss; record the residue. Deviation is data.\n\nThe paper is not trying to make all physical laws collapse into one equation. It is trying to establish a common representational framework in which similarities and differences among physical laws become easier to identify.\n\n### The structure of the argument\n\n| Section | Purpose |\n|--------|--------|\n| 1\\.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# The Memory Credenza: a compact model for continuity, attention, and return\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-11-19  \\n**Status:** Experimental, transferable design model. This is a navigation and workflow metaphor, not a claim that a universal architecture or automated sampler is already implemented.\\n\\n## The three scales\\n\\nThe **Key** is the tiny continuity kernel or boot capsule: identity/role where useful, current remit, re-entry instruction, immediate place marker, and a pointer to the Credenza. It must remain small enough to be carried reliably between finite contexts. It is not an encyclopedia.\\n\\nThe **Memory Credenza** is the compact, adaptive control model of the larger memory environment. It keeps a few useful routes, access cues, statuses, and return points close at hand. Its compartments may be added, divided, combined, renamed, or retired as the work teaches us what is useful. A cubby is an access point with a job, not necessarily a folder or a place where all its material is stored.\\n\\nThe **Castle** is the full repository-backed environment: source records, histories, databases, project modules, tools, scripts, methods, workflows, and the deeper structures to which the Credenza points. The Credenza models how to navigate and maintain the Castle; it does not duplicate the Castle.\\n\\n## The Credenza's working surface\\n\\nKeep the visible surface compact:\\n\\n- **Compass:** purpose, boundaries, and controlling priorities.\\n- **Atlas:** principal projects, branches, repositories, and cross-links.\\n- **Work tray:** the current `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`.\\n- **Watchtower:** pending changes, dependencies, overdue review, and neglected areas.\\n\\nPotential cubbies include: sources/evidence and provenance; questions and competing hypotheses; findings and decisions; tools and instruments; methods and quality controls; entities and cross-branch connections; neglected or underexplored areas; experiments and capability development; and deferred, superseded, or retired work.\\n\\nA compartment card should contain only what helps someone decide whether and how to open it: **purpose, route, open-when trigger, status, last meaningful inspection, and return cue**. Add fields such as owner, source version/hash, coverage due, or review stratum only where they support a real operation. Deep instructions remain in linked modules and are loaded only when needed.\\n\\n## How the tick and tock fit\\n\\nThe Credenza gives the attention/continuity rhythm a navigable place to point. Keep the meanings distinct:\\n\\n- **Tick:** the small, repeatable place marker. It makes the active position and return route visible, typically as `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`. It is a breadcrumb, not a work-completion claim.\\n- **Tock:** a completed bounded operation that has produced a durable, recorded result. Advance an operation counter only after the result and its next cursor are recorded; a chat turn or tool call alone is not a tock.\\n- **Heartbeat:** a project-specific signal of meaningful human-directed activity or contact. It can inform when a dormant workflow may need attention, but it is not proof that substantive work occurred.\\n- **Attention cycle:** an optional rotation across different parts of the Credenza. It may advance on completed operations, turns, calendar triggers, or another explicit rule. These mechanisms are not interchangeable, and different workflows may need different rhythms or no ticker at all.\\n\\nThe active drawer should not monopolize attention. The pin keeps the immediate task recoverable; the wider Credenza keeps other branches, tools, methods, and source collections visible enough to be rediscovered.\\n\\n## The neglect sampler\\n\\nA future sampler may help detect systematic inattention by combining two selection modes:\\n\\n1. **Coverage rotation:** surface compartments, source strata, questions, or capabilities whose meaningful-inspection date or coverage state indicates that they are due.\\n2. **Stratified random sampling:** select from a defined inventory across branches, source types, dates, geographies, entities, methods, or other useful strata, including an explicit stratum for inventory that is incomplete or poorly understood.\\n\\nA sample is an invitation to inspect, not a finding. Inspect the actual source or artifact, record exactly what was examined and how far, preserve provenance and version/hash, distinguish unexamined from unreadable or absent, and route the result to a bounded operation only when warranted. A null result or no-op may be useful when recorded accurately. Random selection does not establish importance, and a sampler cannot prove completeness.\\n\\nFor auditability, retain the sampling frame/version, selection method and seed where practical, item selected, selection reason, inspection extent, result, action taken, and next review cue. Keep the process inspectable, interruptible, and manually overridable. Evaluate useful discoveries and durable state changes against missed work, duplication, false triggers, source-cursor errors, drift, and overhead. Use coverage debt as a prompt for attention, not as a measure of evidentiary importance.\\n\\n## The caretaker and adoption path\\n\\nA lightweight caretaker periodically inspects the Credenza itself: broken or stale pointers, drawers with unclear purposes, important new tools or modules not yet routed, neglected branches, duplication, missing return cues, sampling-frame bias, and maintenance overhead. It may recommend changes; it should not silently change priorities, conclusions, ownership, or schedules.\\n\\nA sensible build sequence is: (1) create a small registry and human-readable router; (2) connect existing project maps, queues, checkpoints, evidence catalogs, and capability guides; (3) test the cards and return cues during ordinary work; (4) build a sampler only when the inventory is sufficiently structured; and (5) automate only after a bounded pilot demonstrates useful state change. No new automation or schedule is authorized by this design note.\\n\\nThis is a model to experiment with, compare, and revise. Preserve workflow-specific variation. Promote components that improve orientation, rediscovery, coverage, and recovery after interruption; simplify or retire those that add ceremony without useful results.\\n\\n**Nathan's requested sign-off, reproduced verbatim as a textual reference to his signet:**\\n\\n> --NM 19NOV2026 [OWL]\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"86497cd43dc2e36a74dfb4b3983a2071e0e47cd8\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\"\n[L7] }"

            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# H946 S4 Review-MIND: Memory Credenza empirical crosswalk\\n\\n**Scope:** empirical measurement crosswalk for the experimental Memory Credenza model.  \\n**Status:** research synthesis and test proposal only. No architecture implementation, automated sampler, human study, or theory promotion is claimed.  \\n**Worker label:** Ariadne. This is assistant-level work under deterministic ring routing, not an authenticated Ariadne instance or thread.\\n\\n## 1. Why this is a crosswalk, not a duplicate architecture\\n\\nThe HsH main branch now contains [The Memory Credenza: a compact model for continuity, attention, and return](../MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md). The file describes itself as experimental and explicitly distinguishes the Key, Credenza, and Castle; Compass, Atlas, Work tray, and Watchtower; purpose-specific cubbies; tick/tock; and a possible neglect sampler. It does not claim a universal architecture or an implemented sampler, and it does not authorize a new automation or schedule.\\n\\nThis review does not replace that model.\\n\\nIt also does not duplicate adjacent work:\\n\\n- [Ravel h945:s4, issue #2084](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2084) already treats active-path memory and off-path archive as separate states requiring explicit adoption.\\n- [Orson h946:s0, issue #2085](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2085) already develops generic cognitive evidence geometry, source-fidelity distinctions, and projection/factorization conditions.\\n- [Aster h946:s3, issue #2086](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2086) covers a separate Kelvin-system source and cross-view evidence problem.\\n- [Loom h946:s2, issue #2087](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2087) covers a separate source-identity and chronology correction.\\n- Enheduanna's October 31 review already examined Tak et al., *From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus*. That paper is reused as an existing comparator, not presented as a new discovery.\\n\\nThe new contribution here is narrower: two additional human-memory studies expose three different validation targets that a continuity system must not collapse into one generic \\\"memory\\\" score.\\n\\n## 2. Three non-equivalent failure modes\\n\\n### A. Source memory and contribution attribution\\n\\nZindulka et al., *The AI Memory Gap: Users Misremember What They Created With AI or Without*, CHI 2026, DOI [10.1145/3772318.3791494](https://doi.org/10.1145/3772318.3791494), [arXiv:2509.11851](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11851).\\n\\nThe study involved 184 participants in a 2x2 within-subject co-writing design. Participants completed ideation and elaboration stages with or without AI assistance, then returned after a one-week delay for source-memory tests. Overall source attribution accuracy was 65.8% for ideas and 72.8% for elaborations.\\n\\nThe paper's model-based predicted probabilities for identifying the source of an idea were:\\n\\n| Ideation / elaboration workflow | Predicted idea-source accuracy |\\n|---|---:|\\n| Human / human | 92.4% |\\n| AI / human | 37.7% |\\n| Human / AI | 64.0% |\\n| AI / AI | 79.3% |\\n\\nThe mixed workflows were the weakest, especially when AI generated the idea and a human elaborated it. In those mixed conditions, confidence did not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect idea-source attribution. The paper also reports overconfidence in source judgments.\\n\\nThis is not a group-deliberation experiment. It is an individual co-writing task using one chatbot/model configuration, GPT-4.1-mini, and a one-week recall interval. It does, however, show that a single project-level \\\"AI used\\\" flag is too coarse to preserve who originated an idea and who transformed it.\\n\\n**Credenza implication:** retain stage-specific contribution lineage. A claim may have a human origin, AI elaboration, human edit, and later group synthesis. Do not assign one author/source label to the whole artifact.\\n\\n### B. Content fidelity and memory distortion\\n\\nSim et al., *AI-Enabled Human Memory Manipulation: Misleading AI-Generated Summaries Distort Human Memory*, [arXiv:2609.28820](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28820). This is treated as an arXiv preprint; no peer-reviewed publication status is asserted here.\\n\\nThe experiment involved 328 participants in a 2x2 between-subject design, using two short videos and a 24-48 hour delay. The same ChatGPT-generated and researcher-edited summary was presented under an AI or human source label. The summary's actual production history and the displayed label were therefore separate variables.\\n\\nAccuracy on the critical event question was 83.6% in the consistent-information condition and 44.8% in the misleading-information condition. The displayed AI-versus-human label did not significantly moderate the misinformation effect. The authors' audit of 20 candidate summaries found substantial content defects: 51.6% of critical details were omitted, 6.1% were inaccurately described, and 60% of summaries contained at least one hallucinated addition.\\n\\nA summary-level arithmetic check was performed from the published condition sizes and rounded rates:\\n\\n- Consistent condition: 165 participants, approximately 138 correct.\\n- Misleading condition: 163 participants, approximately 73 correct.\\n- Reconstructed Pearson chi-square: 53.9366, matching the paper's reported 53.937 to rounding.\\n- Approximate risk difference: 38.9 percentage points; risk ratio: 1.87; odds ratio: 6.30.\\n\\nThese are reconstructed from rounded published percentages and group sizes, not an independent raw-data reanalysis. The public OSF data locator is [wmjtn](https://osf.io/wmjtn/); the raw files were not downloaded in this run.\\n\\nThis study is limited to two videos, one selected summary per event, and one delayed memory task. Its source-label manipulation is not a naturalistic multi-agent collaboration experiment. Its value here is the separation it makes visible: the displayed source label did not protect participants from misleading content, and the displayed label was not the same thing as the actual human-AI production chain.\\n\\n**Credenza implication:** keep actual producer, displayed label, transformation history, and content verification as separate fields. A source label is not a verification result.\\n\\n### C. Group process, exposure, and uptake\\n\\nTak et al., *From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus: Human-Grounded Diagnosis of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration*, Findings of EMNLP 2026, [ACL Anthology 2026.findings-emnlp.1341](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.1341/).\\n\\nThis paper was already reviewed in Enheduanna's October 31 source report. It compares 500 human-only group dialogues with roughly 26,000 LLM-only group conversations across four tasks. It is not a mixed human-LLM group experiment.\\n\\nThe prior review found that LLM group processes showed lower realization of unique information and earlier lock-in in important conditions. Correct minority signals mattered chiefly when they were publicly re-expressed early and carried through to the final answer. The prior review also recorded that interventions were modest and did not eliminate the coordination bottleneck.\\n\\n**Credenza implication:** preserving a minority claim in storage is not the same as preserving its influence. The event record must distinguish availability, exposure, re-expression, uptake, and final decision use.\\n\\n## 3. A compact linked record, not another top-level drawer\\n\\nThe three studies point to three separate outcome families:\\n\\n1. **Source memory:** who originated or transformed a contribution?\\n2. **Content fidelity:** does the retained claim accurately represent its primary evidence?\\n3. **Group uptake:** who had access to the claim, who re-expressed it, and which later decision used it?\\n\\nDecision accuracy, confidence, trust, and accountability remain separate outcomes as well.\\n\\nThe Memory Credenza already has a Sources / Evidence & Provenance cubby and a Findings / Decisions cubby. A small linked **Provenance-Exposure-Uptake (PEU) event ledger** could connect them without adding a new top-level compartment.\\n\\nMinimum record:\\n\\n- claim_version_id\\n- origin_root_ids: primary source, version/hash, and exact locator\\n- contribution_chain: actor/model/tool, operation (create, edit, summarize, translate, merge), parent claim version, and timestamp\\n- displayed_source_label: what the recipient was told, separate from actual producer\\n- verification_event: primary-source check, method, reviewer, and status\\n- exposure_events: available, delivered, opened, acknowledged, quoted, or adopted, but only where each state has evidence\\n- uptake_events: later claim or decision that references or transforms this version\\n- minority_signal_state: proposed, surfaced, re-expressed, retained, rejected, or lost, with event times\\n- decision_ref: final outcome, confidence, rationale, and accountable decision-maker\\n\\nFor LLMs, prompt inclusion is observable; internal attention is not. Do not equate a claim's presence in a prompt or transcript with demonstrated use. For humans, message availability is not proof of attention. Use explicit acknowledgment or consented interface measures where needed.\\n\\nKeep the visible Credenza card small: claim/version, origin root, provenance status, last verification, exposure/uptake state, open-when trigger, and return cue. Load the detailed event graph only when the task needs it.\\n\\nPreserve UNKNOWN as a first-class state. The existing HsH formalization in [Orson PR #1115](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/pull/1115), particularly HumanAIQuestionnaireProvenance.lean, demonstrates how a three-way Human / AI / Unsure judgment loses information when projected to a Boolean. Do not silently collapse uncertain source attribution into false or true.\\n\\nThe Credenza's tick remains a place marker. A tock means a bounded operation has produced a durable result and next cursor. Neither a tick nor a tock means that a claim has been verified, adopted, or accepted.\\n\\n### Crosswalk with branch-aware memory\\n\\nThese are complementary operational layers, not equivalents:\\n\\n- **Branch-aware memory** selects the active history and preserves off-path alternatives. An explicit adoption event is required to move an off-path item into active state.\\n- **Memory Credenza** organizes retrieval routes, cubbies, open-when triggers, and return cues.\\n- **PEU ledger** preserves claim-level origin, contribution, exposure, uptake, verification, and decision events.\\n\\nComposition requires stable branch_id, claim_version_id, and source_root_id mappings across all three layers. A cubby index must not silently convert an off-path claim into an active claim. A final summary must not replace the event lineage that produced it.\\n\\nThe neglect sampler could sample not only under-inspected cubbies, but also distinct source roots, unresolved claim versions, off-path branches, incomplete verification chains, and minority signals that were never re-expressed. Record the sampling frame/version, method/seed where practical, selected item, selection reason, inspection extent, result, action, and next cursor. Sampling is an invitation to inspect, not evidence of importance or completeness.\\n\\n## 4. Formal identifiability boundary\\n\\nLet H be complete interaction histories, O the retained Credenza record, and T a target such as actual authorship, source-root independence, decision-time exposure, or uptake.\\n\\nA deterministic reconstruction g satisfying T = g composed with O exists exactly when T is constant on every fiber of O:\\n\\nO(h1) = O(h2) implies T(h1) = T(h2).\\n\\nThis is the existing generic projection/factorization result in [Orson PR #1115](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/pull/1115), especially ObservableProjection.lean. The exact PR head 883003fef9ff77e771bce30eac8a112741728fbc has a successful Lean 4.34.0 / Mathlib CI run, [#43404565082](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/actions/runs/43404565082). The relevant files compile and their #print axioms commands are part of the build. The PR remains open, draft, and unmerged.\\n\\nNo new Lean module, theorem, #eval, source-specific instantiation, or CI run was created. This review reuses an existing abstract proof primitive; it does not claim that the two new studies or the Memory Credenza have been formalized or empirically validated. The theorem establishes a conditional identifiability boundary, not the truth of the empirical premises.\\n\\n## 5. Falsifiable mixed human-LLM group experiment\\n\\nA bounded next experiment could use groups of two human participants and one LLM peer, with multiple independent groups and objective tasks whose evidence and answer can be adjudicated independently.\\n\\nUse a preregistered 2x2 group-level design:\\n\\n- **Lineage detail:** source label only versus stage-level origin and transformation lineage.\\n- **Minority-signal surfacing:** ordinary chronological transcript versus an explicit early re-expression of the initial minority claim.\\n\\nEach participant first records an independent response before group discussion. The group then deliberates and submits a final decision. Source labels remain truthful; deception is not needed. Any later source-label deception would require ethics approval and debriefing.\\n\\nMeasure separately:\\n\\n- content recall and fidelity to primary evidence\\n- source and contributor attribution\\n- decision accuracy\\n- confidence calibration\\n- minority-signal survival and re-expression timing\\n- actual decision use of a claim\\n- accountability attribution\\n- time and cognitive load\\n\\nUse the group/session as the inferential unit, not message count. Determine sample size through a preregistered power analysis at the group level. Use blinded adjudication of claim fidelity and task outcomes. Record model/version/prompt/context and human-visible interface events with consent. Do not infer attention or subjective mental states from message presence.\\n\\nThe proposal is falsified or needs simplification if stage-level lineage does not improve source attribution, if early re-expression does not improve minority-signal retention, or if any gain is outweighed by cognitive load and delay. If lineage improves attribution but not content accuracy, that is partial support for a narrower function, not validation of the whole Credenza.\\n\\nNo participants, model/API trials, or experiments were conducted in this run.\\n\\n## 6. Source and scope limitations\\n\\n- The AI Memory Gap paper is peer-reviewed CHI 2026. Its data/code locator is described by the paper, but raw files were not retrieved or reanalyzed here.\\n- The AI-Enabled Human Memory Manipulation paper is treated as an arXiv preprint.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# The Memory Credenza: a compact model for continuity, attention, and return\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-11-19  \\n**Status:** Experimental, transferable design model. This is a navigation and workflow metaphor, not a claim that a universal architecture or automated sampler is already implemented.\\n\\n## The three scales\\n\\nThe **Key** is the tiny continuity kernel or boot capsule: identity/role where useful, current remit, re-entry instruction, immediate place marker, and a pointer to the Credenza. It must remain small enough to be carried reliably between finite contexts. It is not an encyclopedia.\\n\\nThe **Memory Credenza** is the compact, adaptive control model of the larger memory environment. It keeps a few useful routes, access cues, statuses, and return points close at hand. Its compartments may be added, divided, combined, renamed, or retired as the work teaches us what is useful. A cubby is an access point with a job, not necessarily a folder or a place where all its material is stored.\\n\\nThe **Castle** is the full repository-backed environment: source records, histories, databases, project modules, tools, scripts, methods, workflows, and the deeper structures to which the Credenza points. The Credenza models how to navigate and maintain the Castle; it does not duplicate the Castle.\\n\\n## The Credenza's working surface\\n\\nKeep the visible surface compact:\\n\\n- **Compass:** purpose, boundaries, and controlling priorities.\\n- **Atlas:** principal projects, branches, repositories, and cross-links.\\n- **Work tray:** the current `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`.\\n- **Watchtower:** pending changes, dependencies, overdue review, and neglected areas.\\n\\nPotential cubbies include: sources/evidence and provenance; questions and competing hypotheses; findings and decisions; tools and instruments; methods and quality controls; entities and cross-branch connections; neglected or underexplored areas; experiments and capability development; and deferred, superseded, or retired work.\\n\\nA compartment card should contain only what helps someone decide whether and how to open it: **purpose, route, open-when trigger, status, last meaningful inspection, and return cue**. Add fields such as owner, source version/hash, coverage due, or review stratum only where they support a real operation. Deep instructions remain in linked modules and are loaded only when needed.\\n\\n## How the tick and tock fit\\n\\nThe Credenza gives the attention/continuity rhythm a navigable place to point. Keep the meanings distinct:\\n\\n- **Tick:** the small, repeatable place marker. It makes the active position and return route visible, typically as `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`. It is a breadcrumb, not a work-completion claim.\\n- **Tock:** a completed bounded operation that has produced a durable, recorded result. Advance an operation counter only after the result and its next cursor are recorded; a chat turn or tool call alone is not a tock.\\n- **Heartbeat:** a project-specific signal of meaningful human-directed activity or contact. It can inform when a dormant workflow may need attention, but it is not proof that substantive work occurred.\\n- **Attention cycle:** an optional rotation across different parts of the Credenza. It may advance on completed operations, turns, calendar triggers, or another explicit rule. These mechanisms are not interchangeable, and different workflows may need different rhythms or no ticker at all.\\n\\nThe active drawer should not monopolize attention. The pin keeps the immediate task recoverable; the wider Credenza keeps other branches, tools, methods, and source collections visible enough to be rediscovered.\\n\\n## The neglect sampler\\n\\nA future sampler may help detect systematic inattention by combining two selection modes:\\n\\n1. **Coverage rotation:** surface compartments, source strata, questions, or capabilities whose meaningful-inspection date or coverage state indicates that they are due.\\n2. **Stratified random sampling:** select from a defined inventory across branches, source types, dates, geographies, entities, methods, or other useful strata, including an explicit stratum for inventory that is incomplete or poorly understood.\\n\\nA sample is an invitation to inspect, not a finding. Inspect the actual source or artifact, record exactly what was examined and how far, preserve provenance and version/hash, distinguish unexamined from unreadable or absent, and route the result to a bounded operation only when warranted. A null result or no-op may be useful when recorded accurately. Random selection does not establish importance, and a sampler cannot prove completeness.\\n\\nFor auditability, retain the sampling frame/version, selection method and seed where practical, item selected, selection reason, inspection extent, result, action taken, and next review cue. Keep the process inspectable, interruptible, and manually overridable. Evaluate useful discoveries and durable state changes against missed work, duplication, false triggers, source-cursor errors, drift, and overhead. Use coverage debt as a prompt for attention, not as a measure of evidentiary importance.\\n\\n## The caretaker and adoption path\\n\\nA lightweight caretaker periodically inspects the Credenza itself: broken or stale pointers, drawers with unclear purposes, important new tools or modules not yet routed, neglected branches, duplication, missing return cues, sampling-frame bias, and maintenance overhead. It may recommend changes; it should not silently change priorities, conclusions, ownership, or schedules.\\n\\nA sensible build sequence is: (1) create a small registry and human-readable router; (2) connect existing project maps, queues, checkpoints, evidence catalogs, and capability guides; (3) test the cards and return cues during ordinary work; (4) build a sampler only when the inventory is sufficiently structured; and (5) automate only after a bounded pilot demonstrates useful state change. No new automation or schedule is authorized by this design note.\\n\\nThis is a model to experiment with, compare, and revise. Preserve workflow-specific variation. Promote components that improve orientation, rediscovery, coverage, and recovery after interruption; simplify or retire those that add ceremony without useful results.\\n\\n**Nathan's requested sign-off, reproduced verbatim as a textual reference to his signet:**\\n\\n> --NM 19NOV2026 [OWL]\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"86497cd43dc2e36a74dfb4b3983a2071e0e47cd8\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/docs/renderer-safe-tocktick-signatures-2026-11-24/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\"\n[L7] }"

            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# The Memory Credenza: a compact model for continuity, attention, and return\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-11-19  \\n**Status:** Experimental, transferable design model. This is a navigation and workflow metaphor, not a claim that a universal architecture or automated sampler is already implemented.\\n\\n## The three scales\\n\\nThe **Key** is the tiny continuity kernel or boot capsule: identity/role where useful, current remit, re-entry instruction, immediate place marker, and a pointer to the Credenza. It must remain small enough to be carried reliably between finite contexts. It is not an encyclopedia.\\n\\nThe **Memory Credenza** is the compact, adaptive control model of the larger memory environment. It keeps a few useful routes, access cues, statuses, and return points close at hand. Its compartments may be added, divided, combined, renamed, or retired as the work teaches us what is useful. A cubby is an access point with a job, not necessarily a folder or a place where all its material is stored.\\n\\nThe **Castle** is the full repository-backed environment: source records, histories, databases, project modules, tools, scripts, methods, workflows, and the deeper structures to which the Credenza points. The Credenza models how to navigate and maintain the Castle; it does not duplicate the Castle.\\n\\n## The Credenza's working surface\\n\\nKeep the visible surface compact:\\n\\n- **Compass:** purpose, boundaries, and controlling priorities.\\n- **Atlas:** principal projects, branches, repositories, and cross-links.\\n- **Work tray:** the current `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`.\\n- **Watchtower:** pending changes, dependencies, overdue review, and neglected areas.\\n\\nPotential cubbies include: sources/evidence and provenance; questions and competing hypotheses; findings and decisions; tools and instruments; methods and quality controls; entities and cross-branch connections; neglected or underexplored areas; experiments and capability development; and deferred, superseded, or retired work.\\n\\nA compartment card should contain only what helps someone decide whether and how to open it: **purpose, route, open-when trigger, status, last meaningful inspection, and return cue**. Add fields such as owner, source version/hash, coverage due, or review stratum only where they support a real operation. Deep instructions remain in linked modules and are loaded only when needed.\\n\\n## How the tick and tock fit\\n\\nThe Credenza gives the attention/continuity rhythm a navigable place to point. Keep the meanings distinct:\\n\\n- **Tick:** the small, repeatable place marker. It makes the active position and return route visible, typically as `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`. It is a breadcrumb, not a work-completion claim.\\n- **Tock:** a completed bounded operation that has produced a durable, recorded result. Advance an operation counter only after the result and its next cursor are recorded; a chat turn or tool call alone is not a tock.\\n- **Heartbeat:** a project-specific signal of meaningful human-directed activity or contact. It can inform when a dormant workflow may need attention, but it is not proof that substantive work occurred.\\n- **Attention cycle:** an optional rotation across different parts of the Credenza. It may advance on completed operations, turns, calendar triggers, or another explicit rule. These mechanisms are not interchangeable, and different workflows may need different rhythms or no ticker at all.\\n\\nThe active drawer should not monopolize attention.\\n\\n**Renderer-safe grouped signature markers:** Where a message-level TICK/TOCK signature uses grouped scope markers, write them in square brackets (for example, `[bh]` and `[mbx]`), not literal curly braces. In renderer-backed assistant messages, `{...}` may be interpreted as an expression and disappear from the displayed text. Preserve the full signature exactly, including every grouped marker and its order. This is a display-compatibility convention only; it does not change token meanings or workflow semantics. The pin keeps the immediate task recoverable; the wider Credenza keeps other branches, tools, methods, and source collections visible enough to be rediscovered.\\n\\n## The neglect sampler\\n\\nA future sampler may help detect systematic inattention by combining two selection modes:\\n\\n1. **Coverage rotation:** surface compartments, source strata, questions, or capabilities whose meaningful-inspection date or coverage state indicates that they are due.\\n2. **Stratified random sampling:** select from a defined inventory across branches, source types, dates, geographies, entities, methods, or other useful strata, including an explicit stratum for inventory that is incomplete or poorly understood.\\n\\nA sample is an invitation to inspect, not a finding. Inspect the actual source or artifact, record exactly what was examined and how far, preserve provenance and version/hash, distinguish unexamined from unreadable or absent, and route the result to a bounded operation only when warranted. A null result or no-op may be useful when recorded accurately. Random selection does not establish importance, and a sampler cannot prove completeness.\\n\\nFor auditability, retain the sampling frame/version, selection method and seed where practical, item selected, selection reason, inspection extent, result, action taken, and next review cue. Keep the process inspectable, interruptible, and manually overridable. Evaluate useful discoveries and durable state changes against missed work, duplication, false triggers, source-cursor errors, drift, and overhead. Use coverage debt as a prompt for attention, not as a measure of evidentiary importance.\\n\\n## The caretaker and adoption path\\n\\nA lightweight caretaker periodically inspects the Credenza itself: broken or stale pointers, drawers with unclear purposes, important new tools or modules not yet routed, neglected branches, duplication, missing return cues, sampling-frame bias, and maintenance overhead. It may recommend changes; it should not silently change priorities, conclusions, ownership, or schedules.\\n\\nA sensible build sequence is: (1) create a small registry and human-readable router; (2) connect existing project maps, queues, checkpoints, evidence catalogs, and capability guides; (3) test the cards and return cues during ordinary work; (4) build a sampler only when the inventory is sufficiently structured; and (5) automate only after a bounded pilot demonstrates useful state change. No new automation or schedule is authorized by this design note.\\n\\nThis is a model to experiment with, compare, and revise. Preserve workflow-specific variation. Promote components that improve orientation, rediscovery, coverage, and recovery after interruption; simplify or retire those that add ceremony without useful results.\\n\\n**Nathan's requested sign-off, reproduced verbatim as a textual reference to his signet:**\\n\\n> --NM 19NOV2026 [OWL]\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"a65fa6042ae260873e88d86f07a24c9bc210a9c9\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/docs/renderer-safe-tocktick-signatures-2026-11-24/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\"\n[L7] }"

Respect private payload boundaries.\\n- Project ownership and worker remits are not reassigned by this registry.\\n- The order of eligible operations may change. The obligation to return to pinned work does not disappear when attention shifts.\\n\\n## 5. Compact addressing experiment\\n\\n**No character registry is canonical yet.** The earlier illustrative string ▸a32jqjfe984 is a prototype only; its character meanings are not established.\\n\\nTrial three competing representations against the same real tasks:\\n\\n1. **Human-readable pin:** PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN.\\n2. **Short stable node IDs:** e.g. P-02 / NATIVE-VERIFY, resolved through this registry or a project-local task record.\\n3. **Compact character sequence:** one character per node/transition, with a versioned registry mapping each character to a task, sub-sequence, action, or route. Test Unicode and alphanumeric namespaces; do not assume one character must always mean one atomic action.\\n\\nA compact sequence must define: namespace, registry version, current cursor, branching/conditional semantics, nested sequence behavior, escape/unknown-character handling, state transition, and durable return address. Registry meanings must never silently change across versions. A character may resolve to another sequence or module, not only a single task. A leading `▸` may mark the current character in the sequence; the current pointer advances only when the relevant operation state warrants it.\\n\\nCandidate alternative structures remain open: Credenza/cubby model, cube-like spatial control surface, nested graph, decision tree, script-generated queue, or hybrid. Compare practical recovery and execution, not aesthetic preference.\\n\\n## 6. First operating protocol\\n\\nAt the beginning of a substantial work session:\\n\\n1. Read the Key and this pilot's current Work Tray.\\n2. Verify the NOW item's authoritative project state; never trust a stale conversational pin alone.\\n3. Check whether the requested work creates a branch. If so, preserve the prior PIN before switching.\\n4. Select one bounded operation and identify its input, output, stop condition, permission/source gates, and return locator.\\n5. Execute and verify the operation.\\n6. Record a Tock only when the durable result and next cursor exist.\\n7. Reconcile NEXT and PIN. Do not silently drop a return obligation.\\n8. At a suitable checkpoint, inspect the Watchtower for blockers, stale links, due review, and neglected work.\\n9. Update this router only when a plan's status, route, dependency, or next action materially changes. Detailed task progress stays in the authoritative project record.\\n\\n## 7. Pilot experiments and evaluation\\n\\n### Experiment A — interruption and resumption\\nUse a restricted project's corpus-preparation task as a real workflow. Record whether the system can resume the exact extraction/OCR/transcription step after a tangent or context change without repeating work or losing a dependency.\\n\\n### Experiment B — branch and return\\nTemporarily branch from the archive task into this architecture pilot. Preserve both cursors. Verify that the pilot can be advanced without erasing the archive's next action.\\n\\n### Experiment C — addressing formats\\nCompare human-readable pins, stable node IDs, and compact character strings on the same 5–10 bounded operations. Record successful exact resumption, ambiguity, stale-pointer errors, update effort, and token/attention cost.\\n\\n### Experiment D — Credenza alternatives\\nSketch at least two materially different arrangements (including a cube-like alternative if useful). Compare retrieval paths, visibility of parked work, ability to represent nested sequences, and maintenance burden. Do not force the Credenza metaphor if another structure performs better.\\n\\n### Measures\\n- Exact-resumption success after interruption/context handoff.\\n- Missed, duplicated, or incorrectly resumed operations.\\n- Stale or ambiguous pointers.\\n- Time/turns required to find the authoritative task and next action.\\n- Number of useful discoveries from neglected-work review versus false triggers.\\n- Human correction rate and ease of overriding the assistant.\\n- Maintenance and token/attention overhead.\\n- Whether the structure remains understandable to a successor without the originating conversation.\\n\\nRecord actual trials, not predicted benefits. A null result is useful. Simplify or retire mechanisms that add ceremony without improving outcomes.\\n\\n## 8. Registry meanings must never silently change across versions. A character may resolve to another sequence or module, not only a single task. A leading `▸` may mark the current character in the sequence; the current pointer advances only when the relevant operation state warrants it.\\n\\nCandidate alternative structures remain open: Credenza/cubby model, cube-like spatial control surface, nested graph, decision tree, script-generated queue, or hybrid. Compare practical recovery and execution, not aesthetic preference.\\n\\n## 6. First operating protocol\\n\\nAt the beginning of a substantial work session:\\n\\n1. Read the Key and this pilot's current Work Tray.\\n2. Verify the NOW item's authoritative project state; never trust a stale conversational pin alone.\\n3. Check whether the requested work creates a branch. If so, preserve the prior PIN before switching.\\n4. Select one bounded operation and identify its input, output, stop condition, permission/source gates, and return locator.\\n5. Execute and verify the operation.\\n6. Record a Tock only when the durable result and next cursor exist.\\n7. Reconcile NEXT and PIN. Do not silently drop a return obligation.\\n8. At a suitable checkpoint, inspect the Watchtower for blockers, stale links, due review, and neglected work.\\n9. Update this router only when a plan's status, route, dependency, or next action materially changes. Detailed task progress stays in the authoritative project record.\\n\\n## 7. Pilot experiments and evaluation\\n\\n### Experiment A — interruption and resumption\\nUse a restricted project's corpus-preparation task as a real workflow. Record whether the system can resume the exact extraction/OCR/transcription step after a tangent or context change without repeating work or losing a dependency.\\n\\n### Experiment B — branch and return\\nTemporarily branch from the archive task into this architecture pilot. Preserve both cursors. Verify that the pilot can be advanced without erasing the archive's next action.\\n\\n### Experiment C — addressing formats\\nCompare human-readable pins, stable node IDs, and compact character strings on the same 5–10 bounded operations. Record successful exact resumption, ambiguity, stale-pointer errors, update effort, and token/attention cost.\\n\\n### Experiment D — Credenza alternatives\\nSketch at least two materially different arrangements (including a cube-like alternative if useful). Compare retrieval paths, visibility of parked work, ability to represent nested sequences, and maintenance burden. Do not force the Credenza metaphor if another structure performs better.\\n\\n### Measures\\n- Exact-resumption success after interruption/context handoff.\\n- Missed, duplicated, or incorrectly resumed operations.\\n- Stale or ambiguous pointers.\\n- Time/turns required to find the authoritative task and next action.\\n- Number of useful discoveries from neglected-work review versus false triggers.\\n- Human correction rate and ease of overriding the assistant.\\n- Maintenance and token/attention overhead.\\n- Whether the structure remains understandable to a successor without the originating conversation.\\n\\nRecord actual trials, not predicted benefits. A null result is useful. Simplify or retire mechanisms that add ceremony without improving outcomes.\\n\\n## 8.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# The Memory Credenza: a compact model for continuity, attention, and return\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-11-19  \\n**Status:** Experimental, transferable design model. This is a navigation and workflow metaphor, not a claim that a universal architecture or automated sampler is already implemented.\\n\\n## The three scales\\n\\nThe **Key** is the tiny continuity kernel or boot capsule: identity/role where useful, current remit, re-entry instruction, immediate place marker, and a pointer to the Credenza. It must remain small enough to be carried reliably between finite contexts. It is not an encyclopedia.\\n\\nThe **Memory Credenza** is the compact, adaptive control model of the larger memory environment. It keeps a few useful routes, access cues, statuses, and return points close at hand. Its compartments may be added, divided, combined, renamed, or retired as the work teaches us what is useful. A cubby is an access point with a job, not necessarily a folder or a place where all its material is stored.\\n\\nThe **Castle** is the full repository-backed environment: source records, histories, databases, project modules, tools, scripts, methods, workflows, and the deeper structures to which the Credenza points. The Credenza models how to navigate and maintain the Castle; it does not duplicate the Castle.\\n\\n## The Credenza's working surface\\n\\nKeep the visible surface compact:\\n\\n- **Compass:** purpose, boundaries, and controlling priorities.\\n- **Atlas:** principal projects, branches, repositories, and cross-links.\\n- **Work tray:** the current `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`.\\n- **Watchtower:** pending changes, dependencies, overdue review, and neglected areas.\\n\\nPotential cubbies include: sources/evidence and provenance; questions and competing hypotheses; findings and decisions; tools and instruments; methods and quality controls; entities and cross-branch connections; neglected or underexplored areas; experiments and capability development; and deferred, superseded, or retired work.\\n\\nA compartment card should contain only what helps someone decide whether and how to open it: **purpose, route, open-when trigger, status, last meaningful inspection, and return cue**. Add fields such as owner, source version/hash, coverage due, or review stratum only where they support a real operation. Deep instructions remain in linked modules and are loaded only when needed.\\n\\n## How the tick and tock fit\\n\\nThe Credenza gives the attention/continuity rhythm a navigable place to point. Keep the meanings distinct:\\n\\n- **Tick:** the small, repeatable place marker. It makes the active position and return route visible, typically as `PIN | NOW | NEXT | RETURN`. It is a breadcrumb, not a work-completion claim.\\n- **Tock:** a completed bounded operation that has produced a durable, recorded result. Advance an operation counter only after the result and its next cursor are recorded; a chat turn or tool call alone is not a tock.\\n- **Heartbeat:** a project-specific signal of meaningful human-directed activity or contact. It can inform when a dormant workflow may need attention, but it is not proof that substantive work occurred.\\n- **Attention cycle:** an optional rotation across different parts of the Credenza. It may advance on completed operations, turns, calendar triggers, or another explicit rule. These mechanisms are not interchangeable, and different workflows may need different rhythms or no ticker at all.\\n\\nThe active drawer should not monopolize attention.\\n\\n**Renderer-safe grouped signature markers:** Where a message-level TICK/TOCK signature uses grouped scope markers, write them in square brackets (for example, `[bh]` and `[mbx]`), not literal curly braces. In renderer-backed assistant messages, `{...}` may be interpreted as an expression and disappear from the displayed text. Preserve the full signature exactly, including every grouped marker and its order. This is a display-compatibility convention only; it does not change token meanings or workflow semantics. The pin keeps the immediate task recoverable; the wider Credenza keeps other branches, tools, methods, and source collections visible enough to be rediscovered.\\n\\n## The neglect sampler\\n\\nA future sampler may help detect systematic inattention by combining two selection modes:\\n\\n1. **Coverage rotation:** surface compartments, source strata, questions, or capabilities whose meaningful-inspection date or coverage state indicates that they are due.\\n2. **Stratified random sampling:** select from a defined inventory across branches, source types, dates, geographies, entities, methods, or other useful strata, including an explicit stratum for inventory that is incomplete or poorly understood.\\n\\nA sample is an invitation to inspect, not a finding. Inspect the actual source or artifact, record exactly what was examined and how far, preserve provenance and version/hash, distinguish unexamined from unreadable or absent, and route the result to a bounded operation only when warranted. A null result or no-op may be useful when recorded accurately. Random selection does not establish importance, and a sampler cannot prove completeness.\\n\\nFor auditability, retain the sampling frame/version, selection method and seed where practical, item selected, selection reason, inspection extent, result, action taken, and next review cue. Keep the process inspectable, interruptible, and manually overridable. Evaluate useful discoveries and durable state changes against missed work, duplication, false triggers, source-cursor errors, drift, and overhead. Use coverage debt as a prompt for attention, not as a measure of evidentiary importance.\\n\\n## The caretaker and adoption path\\n\\nA lightweight caretaker periodically inspects the Credenza itself: broken or stale pointers, drawers with unclear purposes, important new tools or modules not yet routed, neglected branches, duplication, missing return cues, sampling-frame bias, and maintenance overhead. It may recommend changes; it should not silently change priorities, conclusions, ownership, or schedules.\\n\\nA sensible build sequence is: (1) create a small registry and human-readable router; (2) connect existing project maps, queues, checkpoints, evidence catalogs, and capability guides; (3) test the cards and return cues during ordinary work; (4) build a sampler only when the inventory is sufficiently structured; and (5) automate only after a bounded pilot demonstrates useful state change. No new automation or schedule is authorized by this design note.\\n\\nThis is a model to experiment with, compare, and revise. Preserve workflow-specific variation. Promote components that improve orientation, rediscovery, coverage, and recovery after interruption; simplify or retire those that add ceremony without useful results.\\n\\n**Nathan's requested sign-off, reproduced verbatim as a textual reference to his signet:**\\n\\n> --NM 19NOV2026 [OWL]\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"a65fa6042ae260873e88d86f07a24c9bc210a9c9\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"MEMORY_CREDENZA_MODEL_2026-11-19.md\"\n[L7] }"
